Text
Abbreviations

This edition is based on the one in Kāvya-saṅgraha edited by Jīvānanda
Vidyāsāgara. It has been compared with the Motilal Banarsidass edition (1983)
containing the commentary of Arjunavarmadeva. The number in parentheses at the
end of the last line of each verse is the number of the verse in the Motilal
edition. There seems to be a great deal of variation in the order and numbering
of the verses between the editions and the commentators. The order of the verses
found in the Kāvya-saṅgraha forms the backbone of the order of the verses
presented here, even though Arjunavarmadeva considers some of the verses found
in that edition to be interpolations. Those suspect verses have been noted in
the footnotes.

The parentheses in between verses contain citations for the major
anthologies. These have been taken from Sures Chandra Banerji's
edition of Śrīdharadāsa's Sadukti-karṇāmṛta. The abbreviations for those
anthologies are the following:

su. = subhāṣitaratnakoṣa,
sad. = saduktikarṇāmṛta,
subh. = subhāṣitāvalī,
sū. = sūktimuktāvalī,
pad. = padyāvalī,
śā. = śārṅgadharapaddhati
(These equivalences have been taken from the Banerji edition of Sad-ukti-karṇāmṛta and the De edition of Padyāvalī.)
Main Text

jyākṛṣṭibaddhakhaṭakāmukhapāṇipṛṣṭha-
preṅkhannakhāṃśucayasaṃvalito'mbikāyāḥ |
tvāṃ pātu mañjaritapallavakarṇapūra-
lobhabhramadbhramaravibhramabhṛtkaṭākṣaḥ ||1|| (1)

kṣipto hastāvalagnaḥ prasabhamabhihato'pyādadānoṃśukāntaṃ
gṛhṇan keśeṣvapāstaścaraṇanipatito nekṣitaḥ sambhrameṇa |
āliṅgan yo'vadhūtastripurayuvatibhiḥ sāśrunetrotpalābhiḥ
kāmīvārdrāparādhaḥ sa dahatu duritaṃ śāmbhavo vaḥ śarāgniḥ ||2|| (2)
(harabāṇaḥ; su. 49, sad. 76)

ālolāmalakāvalīṃ vilulitāṃ bibhraccalatkuṇḍalaṃ
kiñcinmṛṣṭaviśeṣakaṃ tanutaraiḥ khedāmbhasāṃ śīkaraiḥ |
tanvyā yatsuratāntatāntanayanaṃ vaktraṃ rativyatyaye
tattvāṃ pātu cirāya kiṃ hariharabrahmādibhirdaivataiḥ ||3|| (3)
(viparītaratam- sad. 1141, śā. 3702)

alasavalitaiḥ premārdrārdrairmuhurmukulīkṛtaiḥ
kṣaṇamabhimukhairlajjālolairnimeṣaparāṅmukhaiḥ |
hṛdayanihitaṃ bhāvākūtaṃ vamadbhirivekṣaṇaiḥ
kathaya sukṛtī ko'yaṃ mugdhe tvayādya vilokyate ||4|| (4)
(vāsakasajjā; su. 508; sad. 658)

datto'syāḥ praṇayastvayaiva bhavatā ceyaṃ ciraṃ lālitā
daivād adya kila tvameva kṛtavān asyā navaṃ vipriyam |
manyurduḥsaha eṣa yātyupaśamaṃ no sāntvavādaiḥ sphuṭaṃ
he nistraṃśa vimuktakaṇṭhakaruṇaṃ tāvatsakhī roditu ||5||(6)

likhannāste bhūmiṃ bahiravanataḥ prāṇadayito
nirāhārāḥ skahyaḥ satataruditocchūṇanayanāḥ |
parityaktaṃ sarvaṃ hasitapaṭhitaṃ pañjaraśukais
tavāvasthā ceyaṃ visṛja kaṭhine mānamadhunā ||6|| (7)
(sakhīprabodhaḥ; sad. 713, rasārṇavasudhākara 2.206a)

nāryastanvi haṭhāddharanti ramaṇaṃ tiṣṭhanti no vāritās
tatkiṃ tāmyasi kiṃ ca rodiṣi mudhā tāsāṃ priyaṃ mā kṛthāḥ |
kāntaḥ keliruciryuvā sahṛdayastādṛkpatiḥ kātarae
kiṃ no barkarakarkaraiḥ priyaśatairākramya vikrīyate ||7||(8)

*motīlāla-banārsīdāsa-sampādane (1983):
nāryo mugdhaśaṭhā haranti ramaṇaṃ tiṣṭhanti no vāritās

...
kopātkomalalolabāhulatikāpāśena baddhā dṛḍhaṃ
nītvā keliniketanaṃ dayitayā sāyaṃ sakhīnāṃ puraḥ |
bhūyo'pyevamiti skhalan mṛdugirā saṃsūcya duśceṣṭitaṃ
dhanyo hanyata eva nihnutiparaḥ preyān rudatyā hasan ||8|| (9)
(śaṭhanāyakaḥ, sad. 882, sū. 85.3, subh. 1351)

praharaviratau madhye vāhnastato'pi pare'thavā
kimuta sakale jāte vāhnipriya tvamihaiṣyasi |
iti dinaśataprāpyaṃ deśaṃ priyasya yiyāsato
harati gamanaṃ bālālāpaiḥ sabāṣpagalajjalaiḥ ||9|| (12)
(prasthānabhaṅgaḥ - su. 532, sad. 921, subh. 1048, śā. 3389, sū. 37.7)

yātāḥ kiṃ na milanti sundari punaścintā tvayā matkṛte
no kāryā nitarāṃ kṛśāmi kathayatyevaṃ sabāṣpe mayi |
lajjāmantharatārakeṇa nipataddhārāśruṇā cakṣuṣā
dṛṣṭvā māṃ hāsitena bhāvimaraṇotsāhastayā sūcitaḥ ||10||(10)

dhīraṃ vāridharasya vāri kirataḥ śrutvā niśīthe dhvaniṃ
dīrghocchvāsamudaśruṇā virahiṇīṃ bālāṃ ciraṃ dhyāyatā |
adhvanyena vimuktakaṇṭhamakhilāṃ rātriṃ tathā kranditaṃ
grāmīṇairvrajato janasya vasatirgrāme niṣiddhā yathā ||11||(13)
(varṣāpathikaḥ, sad. 915)

kathamapi sakhi krīḍākopād vrajeti mayodite
kaṭhinahṛdayastyaktvā śayyāṃ balād gata eva saḥ |
iti sarabhasaṃ dhvastapremṇi vyapetaghṛṇe jane
punarapi hatavrīḍaṃ cetaḥ prayāti karomi kim ||12||(15)

dampatyorniśi jalpatorgṛhaśukenākarṇitaṃ yadvacas
tatprātargurusannidhau nigadatastasyopahāraṃ vadhūḥ |
karṇālaṅkṛtipadmarāgaśakalaṃ vinyasya cañcūpuṭe
vrīḍārtā prakaroti dāḍimaphalavyājena vāgbandhanam ||13|| (16)
(śukoktivrīḍā, kuval. 173, su. 621, sad. 1180, subh. 2214, śā. 3743)

ajñānena parāṅmukhīṃ paribhavād āśliṣya māṃ duḥkhitāṃ
kiṃ labdhaṃ caṭula tvayeha nayatā saubhāgyametāṃ daśām |
paśyaitad dayitākucavyatikaron mṛṣṭāṅgarāgāruṇaṃ
vakṣaste malatailapaṅkaśavalairveṇīpadairaṅkitam ||14||(17)
(khaṇḍitā)

ekatrāsanasaṃsthitiḥ parihatā pratudgamād dūratas
tāmbūlānayanacchalena rabhasāśelṣo'pi saṃvighnitaḥ |
ālāpo'pi na miśritaḥ parijanaṃ vyāpārayantyāntike
kāntaṃ pratyupacārataścaturayā kopaḥ kṛtārthīkṛtaḥ ||15|| (18)
(māninī, sad. 692, rasārṇavasudhākara 2.67g)

dṛṣṭvaikāsanasaṃsthite priyatame paścād upetyādarād
ekasyā nayane pidyāya vihitakrīḍānubandhacchalaḥ |
īṣadvakrimakandharaḥ sapulakaḥ premollasanmānasām
antarhāsalasatkapolaphalakāṃ dhūrto'parāṃ cumbati ||16||(19)
(śaṭhanāyakaḥ, su. 603, sad. 881)

caraṇapatanapratyākhyānātprasādaparāṅmukhe
nibhṛtakitavācāretyuktvā ruṣā puruṣīkṛte |
vrajati ramaṇe niḥśvasyoccaiḥ stanasthitahastayā
nayanasalilacchannā dṛṣṭiḥ sakhīṣu niveśitā ||17||(20)
(mānināyakaḥ, sad. 896)

kāñcyā gāḍhatarāvaruddhavasanaprāntā kimarthaṃ punar
mugdhākṣī svaiptīti tatparijanaṃ svairaṃ priye pṛcchati |
mātaḥ svaptumapīha vārayati māmityāhitakrodhayā
paryasya svapiticchalena śayane datto'vakāśastayā ||18||(21)
(śayanādhirohanam, sad. 1094, subh. 2081, sū. 77.11)

ekasmiñśayane parāṅmukhatayā vītottaraṃ tāmyator
anyonyasya hṛdi sthite'pyanunaye saṃrakṣatorgauravam |
dampatyoḥ śanakairapāṅgavalanān miśrībhavaccakṣuṣor
bhagno mānakaliḥ sahāsarabhasaṃ vyāsaktakaṇṭhagraham ||19||(23)
(mānabhaṅgaḥ, sad. 723)

paśyāmo mayi kiṃ prapadyata iti sthairyaṃ mayālambitaṃ
kiṃ māmālapatītyayaṃ khala śaṭhaḥ kopastayāpyāśritaḥ |
ityanyonyavilakṣadṛṣṭicature tasminnavasthāntare
savyājaṃ hasitaṃ mayā dhṛtiharo bāṣpastu muktastayā ||20||(24)
children.translated_text: "Let us see what she resorts to" — with this resolve I held my composure; "Will he speak sweetly to me?" — that rogue, that scoundrel! And so she too took refuge in anger. Then, at that moment of stalemate, both stealing awkward glances with artful eyes, a forced laugh escaped from me — destroyer of all resolve — while from her, tears were set free. ||20||(24)

children.text: (uccāvacaṃ, kuval., 185; sad. 1366)
children.translated_text: (uccāvacaṃ, kuval., 185; sad. 1366)

children.text:
parimlāne māne mukhaśaśini tasyāḥ karadhṛte
mayi kṣīṇopāye praṇipatanamātraikaśaraṇe |
tayā pakṣmaprāntavrajapuṭaniruddhena sahasā
prasādo bāṣpena stanataṭaviśīrṇena kathitaḥ ||21||(25)
children.translated_text: When her <s>māna</s> (sulky pride) had wilted, and her moon-like face rested in her hands, when I was at the end of my stratagems, with prostration my sole remaining refuge, she suddenly declared her forgiveness through tears that spilled down the slopes of her breasts, tears held back at the edges of her eyelashes as in the hollow of cupped palms. ||21||(25)

children.text: (uccāvacaṃ, sad. 1367, subh. 1608, sū. 58.1)
children.translated_text: (uccāvacaṃ, sad. 1367, subh. 1608, sū. 58.1)

children.text:
tasyāḥ sāndravilepanastanataṭapraśleṣamudrāṅkitaṃ
kiṃ vakṣaścaraṇānativyatikaravyājena gopāyyate |
ityukte kva tad ityudīrya sahasā tatsampramārṣṭuṃ mayā
sāśliṣṭā rabhasena tatsukhavaśāttanvyāpi tad vismṛtam ||22||(26)
children.translated_text: "Why do you conceal your chest — stamped with the seal-marks of tight embrace against her breasts thick with ointment — under the pretence of bowing at my feet?" When she said this, I exclaimed "Where is it?" and hastily moved to wipe it away, and in doing so embraced the slender girl with such force that, overcome by that pleasure, even she forgot the matter entirely. ||22||(26)

children.text:
tvaṃ mugdhākṣi vinaiva kañculikayā dhatse manohāriṇīṃ
lakṣmīmityabhidhāyini priyatame tadvīṭikāṃ saṃspṛśi |
śayyopāntaniviṣṭasasmitamukhīnetrotsavānandito
niryātaḥ śanakairalīkavacanopanyāsamālījanaḥ ||23||(27)
bhrūbhaṅge racite'pi dṛṣṭiradhikaṃ sotkaṇṭhamudvīkṣate
kārkaśyaṃ gamite'pi cetasi tanūromāñcamālambate |
ruddhāyāmapi vāci sasmitamidaṃ dagdhānanaṃ jāyate
dṛṣṭe nirvahaṇaṃ bhaviṣyati kathaṃ mānasya tasmiñjane ||24||(28)
children.translated_text:
"You, doe-eyed innocent, wear such captivating beauty even without a bodice," — so saying, the beloved reaches to touch her <s>vīṭikā</s> (betel roll). Seated at the edge of the bed, her face lit with a smile, her eyes a festival of delight, the retinue of attendants slowly withdraws, their pretextual words merely a ruse. ||23||(27)
Though a frown is fashioned upon her brow, her gaze still looks up with ever more longing; though harshness is forced upon her heart, her slender body breaks out in a thrill of goosebumps; though her voice is checked, this scorched face betrays a smile — how then shall <s>māna</s> (pride) be sustained against that man? ||24||(28)

children.text: (anuraktamāninī, su. 695, sad. 702, subh. 1580; uṇ. 5.25)
children.translated_text: (anuraktamāninī, su. 695, sad. 702, subh. 1580; uṇ. 5.25)

children.text: kānte katyapi vāsarāṇi gamaya tvaṃ mīlayitvā dṛśau
children.translated_text: "Beloved, pass however many days you must — just close your eyes,"

children.text: svasti svasti nimīlayāmi nayane yāvan na śūnyā diśaḥ |
children.translated_text: "Blessings, blessings — I shall shut my eyes so long as the horizons are not empty of you."

children.text: āyātā vayamāgamiṣyati suhṛdvargasya bhāgyodayaiḥ
children.translated_text: "We have come back; by the rising fortunes of our dear companions, he shall return too."

children.text: sandeśo vada kastavābhilaṣitastīrtheṣu toyāñjaliḥ ||25||
children.translated_text: "Tell me, what message do you desire — and offerings of water at the holy fords?" ||25||

children.text: (yātrākṣepaḥ, sad.731 (vīrasya))
children.translated_text: (yātrākṣepaḥ, sad.731 (vīrasya))

children.text:
sā patyuḥ prathamāparādhasamaye sakhyopadeśaṃ vinā
no jānāti savibhramāṅgavalanāvakroktisaṃsūcanam |
svacchairacchakapolamūlagalitaiḥ paryastanetrotpalā
bālā kevalameva roditi luṭhallolālakairaśrubhiḥ ||26||(29)
children.translated_text: She, at the first offence of her husband, not knowing — without a friend's instruction — the art of coquettish gestures, sinuous body-turns, and barbed insinuations, the young girl simply weeps, with tears streaming clear from the base of her bright cheeks, her lotus-eyes overturned, her loosened curls tumbling and swaying. ||26||(29)

children.text: (mugdhā; sad.498)
children.translated_text: (mugdhā; sad.498)

children.text:
bhavatu viditaṃ chadmālāpairalaṃ priya gamyatāṃ
tanurapi na te doṣo'smākaṃ vidhistu parāṅmukhaḥ |
tava yathā tathābhūtaṃ prema prapannamimāṃ daśāṃ
prakṛticapale kā naḥ pīḍā gate hatajīvite ||27|| (30)
children.translated_text: "So be it — understood! Enough of your deceitful sweet talk, dear — go! It is not your fault, nor ours — it is fate that has turned away. Your love, such as it was, has come to this state. O fickle one by nature, what grief is there for us when a wretch is gone?" ||27|| (30)

children.text: (māninīvākyam; sad. 708; pad. 223)
children.translated_text: (māninīvākyam; sad. 708; pad. 223)

children.text:
urasi nihitastāro hāraḥ kṛtā jaghane ghane
kalakalavatī kāñcī pādau kvaṇanmaṇinūpurau |
priyamabhisarasyevaṃ mugdhe samāhataḍiṇḍimā
yadi kimadhikatrāsotkampaṃ diśaḥ samudīkṣase ||28||(31)
children.translated_text: A gleaming <s>hāra</s> (pearl necklace) placed upon the breast, a tinkling <s>kāñcī</s> (girdle) fastened on the heavy hips, feet adorned with gem-studded anklets that ring — O innocent girl, if you go to meet your lover thus, with drums practically beating, then why do you gaze at the directions trembling with such excessive fear? ||28||(31)

children.text:
prātaḥ prātarupāgatena janitā nirnidritā cakṣuṣor
mandāyāṃ mayi gauravavyapagamād utpāditaṃ lāghavam |
kiṃ mugdhe na mayā kṛtaṃ ramaṇadhīrmuktā tvayā gamyatāṃ
dusthaṃ tiṣṭhasi yacca pathyamadhunā kartāsmi tacchroṣyasi ||29||(33)
children.translated_text: "Coming to you every morning, I have brought sleeplessness to your eyes; by my languor, through the loss of your reserve, I have produced in you a lightness of reputation. What have I not done to you, innocent one? You have released your lover — go ahead! That you remain in distress — I shall now do what is proper, and you shall hear of it." ||29||(33)

children.text:
sā bālā vayamapragalbhamanasaḥ sā strī vayaṃ kātarāḥ
sā pīnonnatimatpayodharayugaṃ dhatte sakhedā vayam |
sākrāntā jaghanasthalena guruṇā gantuṃ na śaktā vayaṃ
doṣairanyajanāśritairapaṭavo jātāḥ sma ityadbhutam ||30||(34)
children.translated_text: She is a young girl — we are of unpresuming mind; she is a woman — we are timid; she bears a pair of breasts swelling with fullness — we bear only sorrow; she is weighed down by her ample hips and cannot walk — yet we have become unskilled through faults that belong to another person! How astonishing! ||30||(34)

children.text:
(anukūlanāyakaḥ, su. 481, sad. 872, subh. 1346, s.k. 3.42)
prasthānaṃ valayaiḥ kṛtaṃ priyasakhairajasraṃ gataṃ
dhṛtyā na kṣaṇamāsitaṃ vyavasitaṃ cittena gantuṃ puraḥ |
gantuṃ niścitacetasi priyatame sarve samaṃ prasthitā
gantavye sati jīvitapriyasuhṛtsārthaḥ kimu tyajyate ||31|| (35)
children.translated_text:
(anukūlanāyakaḥ, su. 481, sad. 872, subh. 1346, s.k. 3.42)
The bangles have declared their departure, the dear companions — tears — have departed ceaselessly, composure has not stayed even a moment, and the heart has resolved to go on ahead. When the beloved has determined to leave, all set forth together — when departure is certain, why should the caravan of life's dearest companions be abandoned? ||31|| (35)

children.text: (proṣitabhartṛkāvacanam; subh. 1151; śā. 3424; sad. 741; sū. 37.19)
children.translated_text: (proṣitabhartṛkāvacanam; subh. 1151; śā. 3424; sad. 741; sū. 37.19)

children.text:
sandaṣṭādharapallavā sacakitaṃ hastāgramādhunvatī
māmāmuñca śaṭheti kopavacanairānartitabhrūlatā |
śītkārāñcitalocanā sarabhasaṃ yaiścumbitā māninī
prāptaṃ tairamṛtaṃ mudhaiva mathito mūḍhaiḥ suraiḥ sāgaraḥ ||32||(36)
children.translated_text: With her lower lip bitten like a tender leaf, waving the tips of her fingers in alarm, her brow-creeper set dancing by angry words — "Let me go, you cheat!" — her eyes clenched in a hiss of feigned pain, the proud woman who was kissed thus with passion — by those who tasted that nectar, the ocean was churned in vain by the foolish gods. ||32||(36)

children.text: (cumbanam, sad. 1105, subh. 1303, śā. 3668)
children.translated_text: (cumbanam, sad. 1105, subh. 1303, śā. 3668)

children.text:
supto'yaṃ sakhi supyatāmiti gatāḥ sakhyastato'nantaraṃ
premāvāsitayā mayā saralayā nyastaṃ mukhaṃ tanmukhe |
jñāte'līkanimīlane nayanayordhūrtasya romāñcito
lajjāsīn mama tena sāpyapahṛtā tatkālayogyaiḥ kramaiḥ ||33||(37)
children.translated_text: "He is asleep, dear friend — let us sleep too," said the friends, and departed. Then I, artless and overcome with love, placed my face upon his face. When, in those slyly-shut eyes of the rogue, the pretence of sleep was discovered, a thrill ran through him — and shame overtook me, but even that was stolen away by him with methods befitting the moment. ||33||(37)

children.text:
kopo yatra bhrūkuṭiracanā nigraho yatra maunaṃ
yatrānyonyasmitamanunayo yatra dṛṣṭiḥ prasādaḥ |
tasya premṇastad idamadhunā vaiṣamaṃ paśya jātaṃ
tvaṃ pādānte luṭhasi nahi me manyumokṣaḥ khalāyāḥ ||34||(38)
children.translated_text: Where anger is but a knitting of brows, restraint is but silence, where a mutual smile is reconciliation, and a glance is forgiveness — behold what discord has now befallen that love of ours: you grovel at my feet, yet there is no release of my wrath, O faithless man! ||34||(38)

children.text: (nāyake māninī, sad. 709)
children.translated_text: (nāyake māninī, sad. 709)

children.text:
sutanu jahihi kopaṃ paśya pādānataṃ māṃ
na khalu tava kadācitkopa evaṃ vidho'bhūt |
iti nigadati nāthe tiryagāmīlitākṣyā
nayanajalamanalpaṃ muktamuktaṃ na kiñcit ||35||(39)
children.translated_text: "O slender one, abandon your anger — see, I bow at your feet; never before has your anger been of this kind!" As the lord speaks thus, with eyes cast sidelong and half-shut, abundant tears are released, yet not a single word is uttered. ||35||(39)

children.text: (mānabhaṅgaḥ, sad. 725)
children.translated_text: (mānabhaṅgaḥ, sad. 725)

children.text:
gāḍhāliṅganavāmanīkṛtakucaprodbhinnaromodgamā
sāndrasneharasātirekavigalatśrīmannitambāmbarā |
mā mā mānada māti māmalamiti kṣāmākṣarollāpinī
suptā kiṃ nu mṛtā nu kiṃ manasi me līnā vilīnā nu kim ||36||(40)
children.translated_text: Her breasts compressed and flattened by tight embrace, the hair on her body rising in bristling waves, the splendid garment slipping from her hips under the excess flow of dense affection, murmuring with fading eyes — "No, no, O pride-giver, no more, enough, let me be" — is she asleep? Or is she dead? Or has she merged into my heart? Or has she dissolved entirely? ||36||(40)

children.text:
paṭālagne patyau namayati mukhaṃ jātavinayā
haṭhāśleṣaṃ vāñchatyapaharati gātrāṇi nibhṛtam |
na śaknotyākhyātuṃ smitamukhasakhīdattanayanā
hriyā tāmyatyantaḥ prathamaparihāse navavadhūḥ ||37||(41)
children.translated_text: When her husband draws near to the bed-curtain, the new bride modestly lowers her face; she desires his forceful embrace yet shyly draws her limbs away; she cannot speak, and with eyes directed by her smiling friend, she languishes inwardly with shame at this first playful teasing. ||37||(41)

children.text: (navoḍhā; sad. 512, subh. 2056, śā. 3673; viṣṇudās u.ṇ. 5.19)
children.translated_text: (navoḍhā; sad. 512, subh. 2056, śā. 3673; viṣṇudās u.ṇ. 5.19)

children.text:
gate premābandhe praṇayabahumāne vigalite
nivṛtte sadbhāve jana iva jane gacchati puraḥ |
tad utprekṣyotprekṣya priyasakhi gatāṃstāṃśca divasān
na jāne ko heturdalati śatadhā yan na hṛdayam ||38||(43)
children.translated_text: When the bond of love is broken, when the high regard born of affection has crumbled, when true feeling has ceased and he passes before me like a stranger among strangers — imagining and re-imagining, dear friend, those bygone days, I cannot fathom what cause there is that my heart does not shatter into a hundred pieces. ||38||(43)

children.text: (uccāvacaṃ, su. 697, sad. 1368, subh. 1141, śā. 3545, sū. 84.1, rasārṇavasudhākara 2.263c)
children.translated_text: (uccāvacaṃ, su. 697, sad. 1368, subh. 1141, śā. 3545, sū. 84.1, rasārṇavasudhākara 2.263c)

children.text:
ciravirahiṇorutkaṇṭhārtiślathīkṛtagātrayor
navamiva jagaj jātaṃ bhūyaścirād abhinandatoḥ |
kathamapi dine dīrghe yāte niśāmadhirūḍhayoḥ
prasarati kathā bahvī yūnoryathā na tathā ratiḥ ||39||(44)
children.translated_text: For the two long-separated lovers, their limbs loosened by the anguish of yearning, embracing again after so long as though the world were born anew, when somehow the endless day has passed and they have mounted the night, much talk flows between the young pair — but not so much lovemaking. ||39||(44)

children.text:
dīrghā vandanamālikā viracitā hṛṣṭyaiva nendīvaraiḥ
puṣpāṇāṃ prakaraḥ smitena racito no kundajātyādibhiḥ |
dattaḥ svedamucā payodharayuge nārghyo na kumbhāmbhasā
svairevāvayavaiḥ priyasya viśatastanvyā kṛtaṃ maṅgalam ||40||(45)
children.translated_text: A long garland of salutations was offered — not fashioned of blue lotuses but of sheer joy; a heap of flowers was arranged — not of <s>kunda</s> and <s>jātī</s> blossoms but of smiles; the welcoming <s>arghya</s> (oblation) was given — not with water from pitchers but by her perspiring pair of breasts. With her own limbs, the slender woman performed the auspicious welcome for her beloved as he entered. ||40||(45)

children.text:
kānte sāgasi śāyite priyasakhīveśaṃ vidhāyāgate
bhrāntyāliṅgya mayā rahasyamuditaṃ tatsaṅgamākāṅkṣayā |
mugdhe duṣkarametad ityatitarāmuktvā sahāsaṃ balād
āliṅgya chalitāsmi tena kitavenādya pradoṣāgame ||41||(46)
children.translated_text: When my beloved lay sleeping after his offence, I came to him disguised in the garb of a dear friend, and in the darkness he embraced me and joyfully spoke intimate words, driven by longing for union with her. "O innocent girl, this is no easy feat!" he said, and with much laughter forcefully embracing me — I was deceived by that cheat at the onset of evening. ||41||(46)

children.text:
āśaṅkya praṇatiṃ paṭāntapihitau pādau karotyādarāt
vyājenāgatamāvṛṇoti hasitaṃ na spaṣṭamudvīkṣate |
mayyālāpavati pratīpavacanaṃ sakhyā sahābhāṣate
tasyāstiṣṭhatu nirbharapraṇayitā māno'pi ramyodayaḥ ||42||(47)
children.translated_text: Suspecting he will bow in supplication, she modestly covers her feet with the hem of her garment; under some pretext she conceals the laughter that comes unbidden; she does not look at him directly; when I speak to her, she answers indirectly by talking to her friend — let her overflowing affection stand aside, for even her <s>māna</s> (pride) has a charming dawn. ||42||(47)

children.text:
sā yāvanti padānyalīkavacanairālījanaiḥ śikṣitā
tāvantyeva kṛtāgaso drutataraṃ vyāhṛtya patyuḥ puraḥ |
prārabdhā purato yathā manasijasyājñā tathā vartituṃ
premṇo maugdhyavibhūṣaṇasya sahajaḥ ko'pyeṣa kāntaḥ kramaḥ ||43||(48)
children.translated_text: Whatever words her circle of friends had coached her in — those false speeches — just that many accusations she rattled off in rapid haste before her husband, then began to act exactly as the god of love commands. This is some innate and lovely course of love adorned by artless innocence. ||43||(48)

children.text:
dūrādutsukamāgate vivalitaṃ sambhāṣiṇi sphāritaṃ
saṃśliṣyatyaruṇaṃ gṛhītavasane kiñcin natabhrūlatam |
māninyāścaraṇānativyatikare bāṣpāmbupūrṇekṣaṇaṃ
cakṣurjātamaho prapañcacaturaṃ jātāgasi preyasi ||44||(49)
children.translated_text: When the beloved arrives eagerly from afar — an upward flutter; when he speaks — wide-open wonder; when he embraces — a blush; when he grasps her garment — a slight lowering of the brow-vine; when the <s>māninī</s> (proud woman) resists his prostration at her feet — eyes brimming full with tears. Ah, what a master of appearances this eye has become when the lover stands guilty before her! ||44||(49)

children.text:
aṅgānāmatitānavaṃ kathamidaṃ kampaśca kasmātkuto
mugdhe pāṇḍukapolamānanamiti prāṇeśvare pṛcchati |
tanvyā sarvamidaṃ svabhāvajamiti vyāhṛtya pakṣmāntara
vyāpī bāṣpabharastayā calitayā niḥśvasya mukto'nyataḥ ||45||(50)
children.translated_text: "How is there this excessive thinness of limbs? Why this trembling? Whence, O innocent one, this pale-cheeked face?" — when the lord of her life asked thus, the slender woman declared "All this is by nature," but the mass of tears filling the corners of her eyelashes was released with a sigh as she turned away. ||45||(50)

children.text:
purastanvyā gotraskhalanacakito'haṃ natamukhaḥ
pravṛtto vailakṣyātkimapi likhituṃ daivahatakaḥ |
sphuṭo rekhānyāsaḥ kathamapi sa tādṛk pariṇato
gatā yena vyaktaṃ punaravayavaiḥ saiva taruṇī ||46||(51)*asya ślokasya parārdhaḥ:
tataścābhijñāya sphuradaruṇagaṇḍasthalarucā
children.translated_text: Then, upon recognizing [the drawing], with the radiance of her flushed, glowing cheeks,

children.text: manasvinyā rūḍhapraṇayasahasodgadgadagirā |
children.translated_text: the proud woman, with a voice stammering from the surge of deep-rooted love,

children.text: aho citraṃ citraṃ sphuṭamiti nigadyāśrukaluṣaṃ
children.translated_text: exclaiming "Oh wonderful, wonderful — how clear!" with eyes clouded by tears,

children.text: ruṣā brahmāstraṃ me śarasi nihito vāmacaraṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: in anger placed her left foot upon my head like a <s>Brahmāstra</s> (supreme divine weapon). ||

Startled by a slip of name before the slender woman, I, wretched by fate, face downcast, began in embarrassment to draw something on the ground. That clear sketch of lines somehow so transformed that plainly, limb by limb, that very young woman appeared. ||46||(51) *The second half of this verse:

children.text: (gotraskhalitam, sad. 686)
children.translated_text: (<s>Gotraskhalita</s> — the slip of name; <s>Saduktikarṇāmṛta</s> 686)

children.text:
kaṭhinahṛdaye muñca bhrāntiṃ vyalīkakathāśritāṃ
piśunavacanairdukhaṃ netuṃ na yuktamimaṃ janam |
kimidamathavā satyaṃ mugdhe tvayā hi viniścitaṃ
yad abhirucitaṃ tan me kṛtvā priye sukhamāsyatām ||47||(53)
children.translated_text: O hard-hearted one, abandon this delusion born of false tales — it is not right to bring this person to grief through slanderous words. Or else, O innocent one, is this truly what you have determined? Having done what pleases me, O beloved, may you rest happy. ||47||(53)

children.text:
mandaṃ mudritapāṃśavaḥ paripatajjhaṅkārajhañjhāmarud
vegadhvastakuṭīrakāntaragatacchidreṣu labdhāntarāḥ |
karmavyagrakuṭumbinīkucataṭasvedacchidaḥ prāvṛṣaḥ
prārambhe nipatanti kandaladalollāsāḥ payobindavaḥ ||48||*prakṣipto'yaṃ śloka iti arjunavarmadevapādāḥ|
pītastuṣārakiraṇo madhunaiva sārdham
antaḥ praviśya caṣake pratibimbavartī |
mānāndhakāramapi mānavatījanasya
nūnaṃ bibheda yad asau prasasāda sadyaḥ ||49||*rudramadevakumārasya ṭīkāyāmapyeṣa śloko dṛśyate|
(madhupānam, sad. 1089, subh. 2022, śā. 3648)
children.translated_text: At the onset of the rains, raindrops — gently settling the dust, finding entry through crevices of huts in the wilderness torn apart by gusts of buzzing, roaring wind, cooling the sweat on the bosoms of housewives busy with their chores — fall with the exuberance of blossoming <s>kandala</s> (wild jasmine) petals. ||48|| *This verse is interpolated, according to the venerable <s>Arjunavarmadeva</s>.* The moon, having entered the goblet together with the honey-wine, moving as a reflection within — surely it dispelled even the darkness of pride in proud women, for she was immediately appeased. ||49|| *This verse is also seen in the commentary of <s>Rudramadeva</s>.* (Drinking honey-wine; <s>Saduktikarṇāmṛta</s> 1089, <s>Subhāṣitāvalī</s> 2022, <s>Śārṅgadharapaddhati</s> 3648)

children.text:
nabhasi jaladalakṣmīṃ sambhṛtāṃ vīkṣya diṣṭyā
prasarasi yadi kāntetyardhamuktvā kathañcit |
mama paṭamavalambya prollikhantī dharitrīṃ
tadanukṛtavatī sā yatra vāco nivṛttāḥ ||50||*vemabhūpālasya ṭīkāyāmapyeṣa śloko dṛśyate|
iyamasau taralāyatalocanā
gurusamunnatapīnapayodharā |
pṛthunitambabharālasagāminī
priyatamā mama jīvitahāriṇī ||51||*prakṣipto'yaṃ śloka iti arjunavarmadevamahāśayāḥ|
sālaktakena navapallavakomalena
pādena nūpuravatā madanālasena |
yastāḍyate dayitayā praṇayārādhāt
so'ṅgīkṛto bhagavatā makaradhvajena ||52||*vemabhūpālasya ṭīkāyāmeṣa ślokaḥ kevalaṃ labhyate|
(anukūlanāyakaḥ, sad. 873, sū. 85.1)
children.translated_text: Seeing the gathered splendor of rain-clouds in the sky, she began to say "Fortunately, if you would go, O beloved—" but having uttered only half the words with difficulty, clutching my garment, scratching the earth with her toe, she enacted that state where words cease. ||50|| *This verse is also seen in the commentary of <s>Vemabhūpāla</s>.* She of trembling, wide eyes, with full, high, plump breasts, moving slowly under the weight of her broad hips — my beloved, who steals my life away. ||51|| *This verse is interpolated, according to the venerable <s>Arjunavarmadeva</s>.* By that foot adorned with anklets, soft as a fresh sprout, reddened with lac-dye, languid with desire — the one who is struck by his beloved in love's playful anger is honored by the lord bearing the <s>makara</s> (crocodile) banner [i.e., <s>Kāmadeva</s>]. ||52|| *This verse is found only in the commentary of <s>Vemabhūpāla</s>.* (The favorable lover; <s>Saduktikarṇāmṛta</s> 873, <s>Sūktimuktāvalī</s> 85.1)

children.text:
bāle nātha vimuñca mānini ruṣaṃ roṣān mayā kiṃ kṛtaṃ
khedo'smāsu na me'parādhyati bhavān sarve'parādhā mayi |
tatkiṃ rodiṣi gadgadena vacasā kasyāgrato rudyate
nanvetan mama kā tavāsmi dayitā nāsmītyato rudyate ||53||(57)
children.translated_text: "Child!" "Lord!" "Abandon your anger, O sulking one!" "What offense have I committed in my anger?" "You cause me grief!" "I have not wronged you — all faults are mine." "Then why do you weep?" "With a stammering voice, before whom shall I weep?" "But this is mine—" "Who am I to you?" "Beloved!" "I am not!" "Then why do you weep?" ||53||(57)

children.text: (māninī, sad. 691, subh. 1614)
children.translated_text: (<s>Māninī</s> — the sulking woman; <s>Saduktikarṇāmṛta</s> 691, <s>Subhāṣitāvalī</s> 1614)

children.text:
nītvoccairvikṣipantaḥ kṛtatuhinakaṇāsārasaṅgān parāgān
kaundān ānanditālīn atitarasurabhīn bhūriśo diṅmukheṣu |
ete te kuṅkumāktastanakalasabharāsphālanād ucchalantaḥ
pītvā śītkārivaktraṃ śiśuharidṛśāṃ haimanā vānti vātāḥ ||54||*rudramadevakumārasya ṭīkāyāmapyeṣa śloko dṛśyate|
śrutvā tanvyā niśīthe navaghanarasitaṃ viślathāṅkaṃ patitvā
śayyāyāṃ bhūmipṛṣṭhe karataladhṛtayā duḥkhitālījanena |
sotkaṇṭhaṃ muktakaṇṭhaṃ kaṭhinakucataṭāghātaśīrṇāśrubindu
smṛtvā smṛtvā priyasya skhalitamṛduvaco rudyate pānthabadhvā ||55||*rudramadevakumārasya ṭīkāyāmeṣa ślokaḥ kevalaṃ dṛśyate|
śliṣṭaḥ kaṇṭhe kimiti na mayā mūḍhayā prāṇanāthaś
cumbatyasmin vadanavidhutiḥ kiṃ kṛtā kiṃ na dṛṣṭaḥ |
noktaḥ kasmād iti navavadhūceṣṭitaṃ cintayantī
paścāttāpaṃ vahati taruṇī premṇi jāte rasajñā ||56||(58)
children.translated_text: These winter winds — scattering aloft the frost-laden pollen from intensely fragrant <s>kunda</s> (jasmine) flowers that delight the bees in every direction, made fragrant with <s>kuṅkuma</s> (saffron) from bouncing off the pitcher-like breasts of women — blow, having drunk the faces of young doe-eyed women and making them shiver. ||54|| *This verse is also seen in the commentary of <s>Rudramadeva</s>.* Hearing at midnight the rumbling of fresh clouds, the wife of the traveler, falling from the bed onto the bare ground with limbs loosened, supported by the hands of her grieving companion, tears streaming down, shattered against her hard breasts — weeping aloud with throat freed, remembering again and again the soft, faltering words of her beloved. ||55|| *This verse is found only in the commentary of <s>Rudramadeva</s>.* "Why did I not embrace my lord of life when he was at my neck? When he kissed me, why did I turn my face? Why did I not look at him? Why did I not speak?" — thus reflecting on her conduct as a new bride, the young woman, now wise in love's essence, bears her remorse. ||56||(58)

children.text: (uccāvacaḥ, sad. 1369, subh. 2143)
children.translated_text: (Mixed; <s>Saduktikarṇāmṛta</s> 1369, <s>Subhāṣitāvalī</s> 2143)

children.text:
śrutvā nāmāpi yasya sphuṭaghanapulakaṃ jāyate'ṅgaṃ samantāt
dṛṣṭvā yasyānanenduṃ bhavati vapuridaṃ candrakāntānukāri |
tasminnāgatya kaṇṭhagrahaṇasarabhasasthāyini prāṇanāthe
bhagnā mānasya cintā bhavati mama pnarvajramayyāḥ kadā nu ||57||(59)
children.translated_text: He, merely hearing whose name causes the entire body to bristle densely with goosebumps on all sides, seeing whose moon-like face makes this body behave like a <s>candrakānta</s> (moonstone) — when that lord of my life arrives and stands firm, eager to embrace my neck, the resolution of my pride is shattered. When indeed shall it become adamantine? ||57||(59)

children.text:
rāmāṇāṃ ramaṇīyavaktraśaśinaḥ svedodabindupluto
vyālolālakavallarīṃ pracalayan dhunvan nitambāmbaram |
prātarvāti madhau prakāmavikasadrājīvarājīrajo
jālāmodamanoharo ratirasaglāniṃ haranmārutaḥ ||58||*rudramadevakumārasya ṭīkāyāmapyeṣa śloko vartate|
(prābhātikavātaḥ; sad. 459)
children.translated_text: In spring, the morning breeze — flooding the moon-like lovely faces of beautiful women with drops of perspiration, swaying the creeper-like curling locks, fluttering the garments on their hips — blows delightfully, fragrant with clouds of pollen from fully blooming rows of <s>rājīva</s> (blue lotus), carrying away the languor of love's pleasure. ||58|| *This verse is also found in the commentary of <s>Rudramadeva</s>.* (The morning breeze; <s>Saduktikarṇāmṛta</s> 459)

children.text:
aṅgaṃ candanapāṇḍupallavamṛdustāmbūlatāmrādharo
dhārāyantrajalābhiṣekakaluṣe dhautāñjane locane |
antaḥpuṣpasugandhirārdrakavarī sarvāṅgalagnāmbaraṃ
romāṇāṃ ramaṇīyatāṃ vidadhati grīṣmāparāhvāgame ||59||*rudramadevakumārasya ṭīkāyāmapyeṣa śloko dṛśyate|
varamasau divaso na punarniśā
nanu niśaiva varaṃ na punardivā |
ubhayametad upaitvathavā kṣayaṃ
priyajanena na yatra samāgamaḥ ||60||*rudramadevakumārasya ṭīkāyāmeṣa ślokaḥ kevalaṃ labhyate|
lolairlocanavāribhiḥ saśapathaiḥ pādapraṇāmaiḥ priyair
anyāstā vinivārayanti kṛpaṇāḥ prāṇeśvaraṃ prasthitam |
puṇyāhaṃ vraja maṅgalaṃ sudivasaṃ prātaḥ prayātasya te
yatsnehocitamīhitaṃ priyatama tvaṃ nirgataḥ śroṣyasi ||61||(61)
children.translated_text: Limbs pale as sandalwood, soft as fresh sprouts; lips red with <s>tāmbūla</s> (betel); eyes washed of collyrium by the spray of fountain-water; hair within still fragrant with flowers, still damp; garments clinging to every limb — all these create a loveliness of body-hair standing on end at the arrival of a summer afternoon. ||59|| *This verse is also seen in the commentary of <s>Rudramadeva</s>.* Better that day and not the night; nay, better the night and not the day — or rather, let both perish where there is no union with the beloved. ||60|| *This verse is found only in the commentary of <s>Rudramadeva</s>.* Others, wretched, restrain the departing lord of their lives with tremulous tearful eyes, with oaths, with beloved prostrations at his feet. But I, blessed, say: go, may there be auspiciousness, a fair day! What befits my love, O dearest, you shall hear after you have departed in the morning. ||61||(61)

children.text: (yātrākṣepaḥ, sad. 735, s.v. 1060, śā. 3395, sū. 37.12)
children.translated_text: (Obstruction of the journey; <s>Saduktikarṇāmṛta</s> 735, <s>Sūktimuktāvalī</s> 1060, <s>Śārṅgadharapaddhati</s> 3395, <s>Sūktimuktāvalī</s> 37.12)

children.text:
lagnā nāṃśukapallave bhujalatā na dvāradeśe'pitā
no vā pādatale tayā nipatitaṃ tiṣṭheti noktaṃ vacaḥ |
kāle kevalamambudātimaline gantuṃ pravṛttaḥ śaṭhaḥ
tanvyā bāṣpajalaughakalpitanadīpūreṇa baddhaḥ priyaḥ ||62||(62)
children.translated_text: No arm-creeper clung to the hem of his garment; she did not stand at the doorway; nor did she fall at his feet; the word "Stay!" was not uttered. Yet the scoundrel, setting out to leave in the dark, cloud-laden night, was bound by the slender woman's flood of tears that had formed like a river's torrent. ||62||(62)

children.text: (prasthānabhaṅgaḥ, sad. 922, subh. 1057, śā. 3388, sū. 37.5)
children.translated_text: (Prevention of departure; <s>Saduktikarṇāmṛta</s> 922, <s>Subhāṣitāvalī</s> 1057, <s>Śārṅgadharapaddhati</s> 3388, <s>Sūktimuktāvalī</s> 37.5)

children.text:
na jāne saṃmukhāyāte priyāṇi vadati priye |
sarvāṇyaṅgāni me yānti śrotratāṃ kimu netratām ||63||(64)
children.translated_text: I do not know — when my beloved approaches and speaks sweet words, all my limbs become ears. What then of becoming eyes? ||63||(64)

children.text: (nāyikābhilāṣaḥ, sad. 960)
children.translated_text: (The heroine's desire; <s>Saduktikarṇāmṛta</s> 960)

children.text:
virahaviṣamaḥ kāmo vāmastanuṃ kurute tanuṃ
divasagaṇanād akṣaścāsau vyapetaghṛṇo yamaḥ |
tvamapi vaśago mānavyādhervicintaya nātha he
kiśalayamṛdurjīved evaṃ kathaṃ pramadājanaḥ ||64||(67)
children.translated_text: <s>Kāma</s> (Love), cruel in separation, makes the body thin; that merciless <s>Yama</s> (Death), counting the days, waits; and you too are under the power of the hunter who is <s>Māna</s> (pride) — consider this, O lord! How shall women, tender as young shoots, survive thus? ||64||(67)

children.text: (mānināyakaḥ; sad. 898, subh. 1633, śā. 3572)
children.translated_text: (The hero addressing the sulking woman; <s>Saduktikarṇāmṛta</s> 898, <s>Subhāṣitāvalī</s> 1633, <s>Śārṅgadharapaddhati</s> 3572)

children.text:
pādāsakte suciramiha te vāmatā kaiva kānte
sanmārgasthe praṇayini jane kopane ko'parādhaḥ |
itthaṃ tasyāḥ parjanakathā kopavegopaśāntau
bāṣpodbhedaistad anu sahasā na sthitaṃ na prayātam ||65||(68)
children.translated_text: What perversity is there, O beloved, when I have long been devoted to your feet? What offense in a loving person who walks the righteous path? What fault when anger itself is angry? — Thus, when the force of her anger subsided through talk of other matters, tears suddenly broke forth, and she neither stayed nor departed. ||65||(68)

children.text:
purābhūdasmākaṃ niyatamavibhinnā tanuriyaṃ
tato nu tvaṃ preyānvayamapi hatāśāḥ priyatamāḥ |
idānīṃ nāthastvaṃ vayamapi kalatraṃ kimaparaṃ
mayāptaṃ prāṇānāṃ kuliśakaṭhinānāṃ phalamidam ||66||(69)
children.translated_text: Once our bodies were surely undivided as one — hence you are the dearer and I too the most beloved. Now you are lord and I am wife — what more? This is the fruit I have obtained: that my life-breath has become hard as a thunderbolt. ||66||(69)

children.text:
mugdhe mudghatayaiva netumakhilaḥ kālaḥ kimārabhyate
mānaṃ dhatsva dhṛtiṃ vadhāna ṛjutāṃ dūre kuru preyasi |
sakhyaivaṃ pratibodhitā prativacastāmāha bhītānanā
nīceḥ śaṃsa hṛdi sthito nanu sa me prāṇeśvaraḥ śroṣyati ||67||(70)
children.translated_text: O innocent one, why begin to spend the entire time merely in sulking? Maintain your pride, strengthen your resolve, cast straightforwardness far away when your beloved is near! — When thus counseled by her friend, she replied with a frightened face: "Speak softly! My lord of life stands right here in my heart — he will hear!" ||67||(70)

children.text:
pīto yataḥ prabhṛti kāmapipāsitena
tasyā mayādhararasaḥ pracuraḥ priyāyāḥ |
tṛṣṇā tataḥ prabhṛti me dviguṇatvameti
tāvaṇyamasti bahu tatra kimapi citram ||68|| *prakṣipto'yaṃ śloka iti arjunavarmadevamahāśayāḥ|
kva prasthitāsi karabhoru ghane niśīthe
prāṇādhiko vasati yatra janaḥ priyo me |
ekākinī vada kathaṃ na bibheṣi bāle
nanvasti puṅkhitaśaro madanaḥ sahāyaḥ ||69||(71)
children.translated_text: Ever since I, thirsting with desire, drank the abundant nectar of my beloved's lips, my thirst has since doubled — her beauty is so great, what wonder is there in this? ||68|| *This verse is interpolated, according to the venerable <s>Arjunavarmadeva</s>.* "Where are you going, O woman of lovely thighs, in the dense darkness of night?" "Where my beloved resides, dearer to me than life itself." "Alone — tell me, are you not afraid, O child?" "Indeed, <s>Madana</s> (the god of love) with his arrows nocked to the bow is my companion!" ||69||(71)
(<s>Sūktimuktāvalī</s> 816)

children.text:
līlāttāmarasāhato'nyavanitāniḥśaṅkadaṣṭādharaḥ
kaścitkesaradūṣitekṣaṇa iva vyāmīlya netre sthitaḥ |
mugdhā kudmalitānanena dadhato vāyuṃ sthitā tasya sā
bhrāntyā dhūrtatayā ca vepathumatī tenāniśaṃ cumbitā ||70||(72)
children.translated_text: Struck by her playful lotus, his lip bitten without shame by another woman, his eye seemingly stained with pollen — a certain man stood with eyes closed. That innocent one, standing with face like a half-opened bud, was fanning him; out of confusion and his roguishness, she, trembling, was kissed by him ceaselessly. (70)

children.text:
sphuṭatu hṛdayaṃ kāmaṃ kāmaṃ karatu tanuṃ tanuṃ
na sakhi caṭulapremṇā kāryaṃ punardayitena me |
iti sarabhasaṃ mānāṭopād udīrya vacastayā
ramaṇapadavī sāraṅgākṣyā saśaṅkitamīkṣitā ||71|| (73)
children.translated_text: 'Let my heart burst if it will! Let desire make my body ever thinner! But no more, my friend, shall I have dealings with that fickle lover!' — Having uttered these words impetuously from the swell of her jealous pride, the path of her beloved was watched with anxious eyes by that doe-eyed woman. (71)

children.text: (anuraktamāninī; su. 666, sad. 705, sū. 55.1)
children.translated_text: (The loving woman in jealous anger; <s>Subhāṣitāvalī</s> 666, <s>Saduktikarṇāmṛta</s> 705, <s>Sūktimuktāvalī</s> 55.1)

children.text:
gāḍhāśleṣaviśīrṇacandanarajaḥpuñjaprakarṣādiyaṃ
śayyā samprati komalāṅgi paruṣetyāropya māṃ vakṣasi |
gāḍhauṣṭhagrahapūrvamākulatayā pādāgrasaṃdaṃśake-
nākṛṣyāmbaramātmano yaducitaṃ dhūrtena tatprastutam ||72||(74)
children.translated_text: 'This bed is now rough, O soft-limbed one, because the sandal-paste has been scattered by our tight embrace' — placing me upon his chest [with these words], with a deep bite on the lips, in agitation, pulling at my garment-edge with his toes — what was fitting [for love] was initiated by that rogue. (72)

children.text:
kathamapi kṛtapratyākhyāne priye skhalitottare
virahakṛśayā kṛtvā vyājaṃ prakalpitamaśrutaṃ |
asahanasakhīśrotraprāptipramādasasaṃbhramaṃ
vigalitadṛśā śūnye gehe samucchvasitaṃ punaḥ ||73||(75)
children.translated_text: When the beloved was somehow refused, and his replies faltered, the woman, emaciated by separation, devised a pretended excuse — something fabricated, unheard of — with flurried alarm at the prospect of her intolerant friend overhearing — and with tears flowing, in the empty house, she sighed again. (73)

children.text:
ādṛṣṭiprasarātpriyasya padavīmudvīkṣya nirviṇṇayā
vicchinneṣu pathiṣvahaḥpariṇatau dhvānte samutsarpati |
dattaikaṃ saśucā gṛhaṃ prati padaṃ pānthastriyāsminkṣaṇe
mā bhūdāgata ityamandavalitagrīvaṃ punarvīkṣitam ||74||(76)
children.translated_text: Having gazed along the road of her beloved as far as the eye could reach, the disheartened woman, when the paths were cut off and darkness crept over the waning day, took one step toward home with grief — and at that moment, lest the traveler have returned, she looked back again with neck fully turned. (74)

children.text:
āyāte dayite manorathaśatairnītvā kathaṃciddinaṃ
vaidagdhyāpagamājjaḍe parijane dīrghāṃ kathāṃ kurvati |
daṣṭāsmītyabhidhāya satvarapadaṃ vyādhūya cīnāṃśukaṃ
tanvaṅgyā ratikātareṇa manasā nītaḥ pradīpaḥ śamam ||75||(77)
children.translated_text: When the beloved arrived, having somehow passed the day with a hundred fantasies, and the servants, having lost all cleverness, stupidly carried on a long conversation — saying 'I've been bitten [by something]!' and stepping swiftly, she shook off her silk garment; and the lamp was extinguished by the slender-bodied woman's mind, eager with passion for love. (75)

children.text:
ālambyāṅgaṇavāṭikāparisare cūtadrume mañjarīṃ
sarpatsāndraparāgalampaṭaraṭadbhṛṅgāṅganāśobhinīm |
manye svāṃ tanumuttarīyaśakalenācchādya bālā sphurat-
kaṇṭhadhvānanirodhakampitakucaśvāsodgamā roditi ||76||(78)
children.translated_text: Grasping a mango blossom in the courtyard garden, beautiful with the splendor of bees humming greedily amid thick swirling pollen — I think the young girl, covering her own body with a corner of her upper cloth, weeps with heaving breasts and rising breath, suppressing the sound swelling in her throat. (76)

children.text:
yāsyāmiti samudyatasya gaditaṃ visrabdhamākarṇitaṃ
gacchandūramupekṣito muhurasau vyāvṛtya tiṣṭhannapi |
tacchūnye punarāsthitāsmi bhavane prāṇāsta ete dṛḍhāḥ
sakhyastiṣṭhata jīvitavyasaninī dambhādahaṃ rodimi ||77||(79)
children.translated_text: 'He will go!' — his announcement was trustingly heard; going far, he was ignored; turning back and standing still repeatedly — 'Now he is gone, and I am here in this empty house. My life-breaths are strong. Friends, stay — I, who crave to live, weep only out of pretense.' (77)

children.text:
śūnyaṃ vāsagṛhaṃ vilokya śayanādutthāya kiṃcicchanair
nidrāvyājamupāgatasya suciraṃ nirvarṇya patyurmukham ||
children.translated_text: Having seen the empty bedchamber and risen somewhat slowly from the bed, having gazed long at the face of her husband who had come back pretending to be asleep,

children.text:
visrabdhaṃ paricumbya jātapulakāmālokya gaṇḍastalīṃ
lajjānamramukhī priyeṇa hasatā bālā ciraṃ cumbitā ||78||(82)
children.translated_text: Having kissed him trustingly, seeing his cheek covered with goosebumps, the young woman, her face bowed with shyness, was kissed for a long time by her laughing beloved. (78)

children.text:
loladbhrūlatayā vipakṣadigupanyāse'vadhūtaṃ śiras
tadvṛttāntanirīkṣaṇe kṛtanamaskāro vilakṣaḥ sthitaḥ |
kopāttāmrakapolabhittini mukhe dṛṣṭyā gataḥ pādayor
utsṛṣṭo gurusannidhāvapi vidhirdvābhyāṃ na kālocitaḥ ||79||(83)
children.translated_text: At the sidelong glance of her darting eyebrow toward the rival's direction, the head was shaken [in denial]; at the inspection of the matter, he stood embarrassed, having made an [awkward] bow. His gaze went to her feet on seeing her face flushed copper-red with anger — he was released [from her anger] even in the presence of the elders — an act not timely for either of them. (79)

children.text:
jātā notkalikā stanau na lulitau gātraṃ na romāñcitaṃ
vaktraṃ svedakaṇānvita na sahasā yāvacchaṭhenāmunā |
dṛṣṭenāva mano hṛtaṃ dhṛtimuṣā prāṇeśvareṇādya me
tatkenātra nirūpyamāṇanipuṇo mānaḥ samādhīyatām ||80||(84)
children.translated_text: 'No throbbing arose, my breasts were not fondled, my body did not bristle with goosebumps, my face was not suddenly covered with beads of sweat — yet today my mind has been stolen merely by seeing that rogue, that thief of composure, that lord of my life. Who here can determine the truth? Let me compose a fitting jealous anger!' (80)

children.text:
dṛṣṭaḥ kātaranetrayā cirtaraṃ baddhāñjaliṃ yācit
paścādaṃśukapallavena vidhṛto nirvyājamāliṅgitaḥ |
ityākṣipya yadā samastamaghṛṇo gantuṃ pravṛttaḥ śaṭhaḥ
pūrvaṃ prāṇaparigraho dayitayā muktastato vallabhaḥ ||81||(85)
children.translated_text: Gazed at long with timid eyes, implored with folded palms, afterward held back by the hem of her garment, embraced without pretense — yet having cast aside all this, the merciless rogue set out to go. First the beloved released her grip on his life [-breath]; then [she released] her beloved. (81)

children.text:
kṛto dūrādeva smitamadhuramabhyudgamavidhiḥ
śirasyājñā nyastā prativacanavatyānatimati |
na dṛṣṭeḥ śaithilyaṃ milana iti ceto dahati me
nigūḍhāntaḥkopātkaṭhiṇahṛdaye saṃvṛtiriyam ||82||(14)
children.translated_text: From afar he performed the greeting with a sweet smile; on his head the command was placed with a reply of bowed submission; there was no slackening of the gaze at the meeting — this burns my heart. Through concealed inner anger, the hard-hearted one maintains this composure. (82)

children.text:
ekasmiñśayane vipakṣaramaṇīnāmagrahe mugdhayā
sadyaḥ kopaparāṅmukhaṃ śayitayā cāṭūni kurvannapi |
āvegādavadhīritaḥ priyatamastūṣṇīṃ sthitastatkṣaṇāt
mā bhūssupta ivaiṣa mandavalitagrīvaṃ punarvīkṣitaḥ ||83||(22)
children.translated_text: On the same bed, when the innocent woman, hearing the name of her rival, had angrily turned away and lain down, and though he made flattering speeches, she, in her agitation, pushed away her most beloved, who then stood silent — at that very moment, 'Is he perhaps asleep?' — she looked back with neck gently turned. (83)

children.text:
malayamarutāṃ vrātā yātā vikāsitamallikā
parimalabharo bhagno grīṣmastvamutsahase yadi |
ghana ghaṭayituṃ nisnehaṃ tvāṃ ya eva nivartane
prabhavati gavāṃ kinnaśchinnaṃ sa eva dhanañjayaḥ ||84||(32)
children.translated_text: 'The troops of <s>Malaya</s> breezes have gone, the <s>mallikā</s> jasmine in bloom — its fragrance-load is broken, summer is ended — if you wish, O cloud, to unite [with the earth]. But he who has the power to turn back the heartless you — is that same <s>Dhanañjaya</s> (fire/Arjuna) who sundered the herds of cattle.' (84)

children.text:
svaṃ dṛṣṭvā karajakṣataṃ madhumadakṣīvā vicāryerṣyayā
gacchantī kva nu gacchasīti vidhṛtā bālā paṭānte mayā |
pratyāvṛttamukhī sabāṣpanayanā māṃ muñca muñceti sā
kopātprasphuritādharā yadavadattatkena vismaryate ||85||(55)
children.translated_text: Seeing her own nail-scratches [on the lover's body], intoxicated with passion's wine, examining them with jealousy — as she went away, 'Where are you going?' — she was seized by me at the hem of her garment. That young woman, turning her face, eyes brimming with tears, 'Release me! Release me!' — trembling with anger on her quivering lip, what she said then — who could forget? (85)

children.text:
sālaktakaṃ śatadalādhikakāntiramyaṃ
ratnaughadhāmanikarāruṇanūpuraṃ ca |
kṣiptaṃ bhṛśaṃ kupitayā taralotpalākṣyā
saubhāgyacihnamiva mūrdhni padaṃ vireje ||86|| *prakṣipto'yaṃ śloka iti arjunavarmadevamahāśayāḥ|
kapole patrālī karatalanirodhena mṛditā
nipīto niḥśvāsairayamamṛtahṛdyo'dhararasaḥ |
muhuḥ kaṇṭhe lagnastaralayati bāṣpaḥ stanataṭaṃ
priyo manyurjātastava niranurodhe na tu vayam ||87|| (81)
children.translated_text:
Adorned with lac-dye, lovelier than a hundred-petaled lotus, reddened with anklets radiant with heaps of jewels — the foot, kicked hard by the restless-lotus-eyed woman in anger, shone upon his head like a mark of good fortune. (86) [*This verse is considered an interpolation by <s>Arjunavarmadeva</s>.]
The leaf-ornament on the cheek was crushed by the pressure of his palm; this nectar-sweet lower lip was drunk in through his breaths; tears choke the throat repeatedly and make the breast-slope heave — 'My dear, your anger has arisen, but not from indifference — and neither have I [been unfaithful].' (87)

children.text: (anunayaḥ, su. 664, sad. 720, s.k.v. 489, subh. 1627)
children.translated_text: (Conciliation; <s>Subhāṣitāvalī</s> 664, <s>Saduktikarṇāmṛta</s> 720, <s>Subhāṣitaratnakoṣa</s> 489, <s>Subhāṣitāvali</s> 1627)

children.text:
lākṣālakṣmalalāṭapaṭṭamabhitaḥ keyūramudrā gale
vaktre kajjalakālimā nayanayorstāmbūlarāgo ghanaḥ |
dṛṣṭā kopavidhāyi maṇḍanamidaṃ prātaściraṃ preyaso
līlātāmarasodare mṛgadṛśaḥ śvāsāḥ samāptiṃ gatāḥ ||88|| (60)
children.translated_text: The lac-mark on the forehead, the armlet-imprint on the neck, the collyrium-darkness on the face, the dense betel-redness on the eyes — seeing early in the morning this anger-provoking adornment on her beloved's lotus-belly, the deer-eyed woman's sighs reached their end. (88)

children.text:
(anyaraticihnaduḥkhitā; sad. 594; śā. 3740, subh. 2215; sū. 82.17; pad. 222; daśarūpaka 2.6)
tapte mahāvirahavahniśikhāvalībhir
āpāṇḍurastanataṭe hṛdaye priyāyāḥ |
rathyālivīkṣaṇaniveśitaloladṛṣṭer
nūnaṃ chanacchaniti bāṣpakaṇāḥ patanti ||89||(86)
children.translated_text:
(She who is pained by signs of love with another; <s>Saduktikarṇāmṛta</s> 594; <s>Śārṅgadharapaddhati</s> 3740, <s>Subhāṣitāvali</s> 2215; <s>Sūktimuktāvalī</s> 82.17; <s>Padyāvalī</s> 222; <s>Daśarūpaka</s> 2.6)
Burnt by the flame-rows of the great fire of separation, the breast-slope and heart of the beloved are pale and wan; she who fixes her restless gaze upon the street, watching — surely, 'drip, drip,' tear-drops fall. (89)

children.text:
cintāmohaviniścalena manasā maunena pādānataḥ
pratyākhyānaparāṅmukhaḥ priyatamo gantuṃ pravṛtto'dhunā |
savrīḍairalasairnirantaraluṭhadbāṣpākulairlocanaiḥ
śvāsotkampakucaṃ nirīkṣya suciraṃ jīvāśayā vāritaḥ ||90||(87)
children.translated_text: With his mind motionless from thought and bewilderment, silent, bowed at her feet, turned away from her refusal — the most beloved was now setting out to go. With shy, listless eyes, continuously rolling with tear-blurred confusion, with breasts heaving from sighs — gazing at him long with hope of life, she restrained him. (90)

children.text:
tanvaṅgyā gurusannidhau nayanajaṃ yad vāri saṃstambhitaṃ
tenāntargalitena manmathaśikhī sikto'nuṣaṅgodbhavaḥ |
manye tasya nirasyamānakiraṇasyaiṣā mukhenodgatā
śvāsāmodasamākulālinikaravyājena dhūmāvaliḥ ||91||(96)
children.translated_text: The tears born from the eyes of the slender-bodied woman that were suppressed in the presence of the elder — by those, flowing inwardly, the fire of desire, born of attachment, was watered. I think, of that [fire] whose rays were being driven away, this is the row of smoke that issued from her mouth — in the guise of swarms of bees stirred by the fragrance of her sighs. (91)

children.text:
bhrūbhedo racitaḥ ciraṃ nayanayorabhyastamāmīlanaṃ
roddhuṃ śikṣitamādareṇa hasitaṃ maune'bhiyogaḥ kṛtaḥ |
dhairyaṃ kartumapi sthirīkṛtamidaṃ cetaḥ kathañcin mayā
baddho mānaparigrahe parikaraḥ siddhistu daivasthitā ||92||(97)*rūpagosvāmipādasya padyāvalyām (231) etasya ślokasyaiṣa rūpaḥ:
bhrūbhaṅgo guṇitaściraṃ nayanayorabhyastamāmīlanaṃ
children.translated_text: The brow-knitting was repeated, the closing of the eyes was long rehearsed,

children.text: roddhuṃ śikṣitamādareṇa hasitaṃ maune'bhiyogaḥ kṛtaḥ |
children.translated_text: The suppression of laughter was carefully trained, and effort was applied to silence;

children.text: dhairyaṃ kartumapi sthirīkṛtamidaṃ cetaḥ kathañcin mayā
children.translated_text: Somehow I steadied this mind to maintain composure —

children.text: baddho mānaparigrahe parikaraḥ siddhistu daive sthitā ||
children.translated_text: The girdle was fastened for the custody of jealous pride — but success rests with fate.

The knitting of the brows was practiced, the closing of the eyes was long rehearsed, the suppression of laughter was carefully trained, and effort was applied to silence. Somehow I steadied this mind to maintain composure — the girdle was fastened for the custody of jealous pride — but success rests with fate. (92) [*In <s>Rūpa Gosvāmin</s>'s <s>Padyāvalī</s> (231) this verse has this form:]

children.text: (anuraktamāninī, su. 645, sad. 703, pad. 231)
children.translated_text: (The loving woman in jealous anger; <s>Subhāṣitāvalī</s> 645, <s>Saduktikarṇāmṛta</s> 703, <s>Padyāvalī</s> 231)

children.text:
deśairantaritā śataiśca saritāmurvībhṛtāṃ kānanair
yatnenāpi na yāti locanapathaṃ kānteti jānannapi |
udgrīvaścaraṇārdharuddhavasudhaḥ kṛtvāśrupūrṇāṃ dṛśaṃ
tāmāśāṃ pathikastathāpi kimapi dhyāyaṃściraṃ vīkṣate ||93|| (99)
children.translated_text: Separated by lands and by hundreds of rivers, mountains, and forests — knowing well that his beloved does not enter the path of his eyes even with effort — the traveler, with outstretched neck, one foot half-pressing the earth, with eyes brimming with tears, still gazes long toward that direction, contemplating something. (93)

children.text: (proṣitaḥ, su. 765, sad. 901, śā. 3445)
children.translated_text: (The one whose beloved has departed; <s>Subhāṣitāvalī</s> 765, <s>Saduktikarṇāmṛta</s> 901, <s>Śārṅgadharapaddhati</s> 3445)

children.text:
mlānaṃ pāṇḍu kṛśaṃ viyogavidhuraṃ lambālakaṃ sālasaṃ
bhūyastatkṣaṇajātakānti rabhasaprāpte mayi proṣite |
sāṭopaṃ ratikelikālasarasaṃ ramyaṃ kimapyādarād
yatpītaṃ sutanormayā vadanakaṃ vaktuṃ na tatpāryate ||94||(88)
children.translated_text: Wilted, pallid, emaciated, distraught with separation, with drooping locks, listless — yet at the instant of my hurried return from abroad, suddenly radiant with beauty — that face of my slender wife, drunk by me with passionate delight, a love-sport lingering and languid — that cannot be described. (94)

children.text:
saivāhaṃ pramadā nṛṇāmadhigatāvetau ca tau nūpurāv
eṣāsmākamavṛttireva sahajavrīḍādhanaḥ strījanaḥ |
itthaṃ lajjitayā smṛterupagame matvā tanuṃ sambhramāt
pumbhāvaḥ prathamaṃ rativyatikare muktastato vallabhaḥ ||95||(89)
children.translated_text: 'I am that same woman attainable by men, and these are those same anklets; we women are by nature thus — with modesty as our only wealth.' In this way, when the memory arose and she became bashful, he thought [her embarrassment genuine] and in his eagerness, the male state first dissolved during the act of love — then [she embraced] her beloved. // 95 // (89)

children.text:
karakisalayaṃ dhūtvā dhūtvā vimārgati vāsasī
kṣipati sumanomālāśeṣaṃ pradīpaśikhāṃ prati |
sthagayati muhuḥ patyurnetre vihasya samākulā
surataviratā ramyā tanvī muhurmuhurīkṣate ||96||(90)
children.translated_text: Shaking and shaking the tender sprout-like hand, she searches for her garments; she flings the remaining flower garland toward the lamp's flame; she repeatedly covers her husband's eyes, laughing and flustered — the lovely slender woman, having finished lovemaking, gazes again and again. // 96 // (90)

children.text:
santyevātra gṛhe gṛhe yuvatayastāḥ pṛccha gatvādhunā
preyāṃsaḥ praṇamanti kiṃ tava punardāso yathā vartate |
ātmadrohiṇi durjanaiḥ pralapitaṃ karṇe'niśaṃ mā kṛthāś
chinnasneharasā bhavanti puruṣā duḥkhānuvartyāḥ punaḥ ||97||(91)
children.translated_text: 'There are indeed young women in every house — go and ask them now: do the lovers bow down to you as your servant does?' O self-harming one, do not heed what malicious people constantly whisper in your ear — men whose affection has dried up become indifferent; but they follow suffering [back to love]. // 97 // (91)

children.text:
niḥśvāsā vadanaṃ dahanti hṛdayaṃ nirmūlamunmathyate
nidrā neti na dṛśyate priyamukhaṃ rātrindivaṃ rudyate |
aṅgaṃ śoṣamupaiti pādapatitaḥ preyāṃstathopekṣitaḥ
sakhyaḥ kaṃ guṇamākalayya dayite mānaṃ vayaṃ kāritāḥ ||98|| (92)
children.translated_text: Sighs burn the face, the heart is uprooted and churned, sleep does not come, the face of the beloved is not seen, day and night there is weeping, the body wastes away, the beloved has fallen at my feet yet is ignored — O friends, having calculated what merit [accrues], for what reason have we been made to maintain our pride toward the beloved? // 98 // (92)

children.text: (pad. 237, sad. 677; daśarūpaka 2.26)
children.translated_text: (<s>Padyāvalī</s> 237, <s>Saduktikarṇāmṛta</s> 677; <s>Daśarūpaka</s> 2.26)

children.text:
adyārabhya yadi priye punarahaṃ mānasya vā'nyasya vā
gṛhṇīyāṃ śaṭhadurnayena manasā nāmāpi saṃkṣepataḥ |
tattenaiva vinā śaśāṅkadhavalāḥ spaṣṭāṭṭahāsā niśā
eko vā divasaḥ payodamalino yāyānmama prāvṛṣi ||99||(93)
children.translated_text: 'From this day forth, if I should ever again, even in brief, take up the very name of pride or anything else with a deceitful and wicked mind — then without her alone may the nights, white as moonlight, pass with loud laughter, or may even a single rain-clouded day of the monsoon pass for me.' // 99 // (93)

children.text:
idaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ priyatama tanu śvetamatha kiṃ
gamiṣyāmo yāmo bhavatu gamanenātha bhavatu |
purā yenāvaṃ me ciramanusṛtā cittapadavī
sa evānyo jātaḥ sakhi paricitāḥ kasya puruṣāḥ ||100||(94)
children.translated_text: 'This is dark, dark, O dearest — is this body then white? Shall we go? Let us go — let it be with going, or let it be [without].' He who once thus long followed the path of my heart has now become a stranger — O friend, whose are these men who were once so intimate? // 100 // (94)

children.text:
caraṇapatanaṃ sakhyālāpā manoharacāṭavaḥ
kṛśataratanorgāḍhāśleṣo haṭhātparicumbanam |
iti hi capalo mānārambhastathāpi hi notsahe
hṛdayadayitaḥ kāntaḥ kāmaṃ kimatra karomyaham ||101||(95)
children.translated_text: Falling at [my] feet, the conversations of friends, charming sweet words, the tight embrace of [his] ever more emaciated body, a forceful kiss — thus indeed the onset of pride is fickle; yet I cannot [resist] — the beloved is dear to [my] heart; let desire do what it will — what can I do about it? // 101 // (95)

children.text:
ahaṃ tenāhūtā kimapi kathayāmīti vijane
samīpe cāsīnā sarasahṛdayatvādavahitā |
tataḥ karṇopānte kimapi vadatāghrāya vadanaṃ
gṛhītā dharmille sakhi sa ca mayā gāḍhamadhare ||102||(98)
children.translated_text: 'I was called by him; I shall say something,' — thus in a secluded place, sitting near [him], I was attentive due to the tenderness of [my] heart. Then, as he whispered something at my ear and smelled my face, O friend, he was seized by [me] at his hair — and he [seized] me firmly at the lip. // 102 // (98)

children.text:
cakṣuḥprītiprasakte manasi paricaye cintyamānābhyupāye
rāge yāte'tibhūmiṃ vikasati sutarāṃ gocare dūtikāyāḥ |
āstāṃ dūreṇa tāvatsarabhasadayitāliṅganānandalābhas
tadgehopāntarathyābhramaṇamapi parāṃ nirvṛtiṃ santanoti ||103||(100)
children.translated_text: When the mind is absorbed in the delight of the eyes, when intimacy has grown, when the stratagem is being contemplated, when passion has gone to its extreme, when [the affair] has fully blossomed into the domain of a go-between — let alone the joy of the impetuous embrace of the beloved from afar; even wandering in the lane near her house bestows supreme bliss. // 103 // (100)

children.text:
kānte talpamupāgate vigalitā nīvī svayaṃ bandhanād
vāso viślathamekhalāguṇadhṛtaṃ kiṃcinnitambe sthitam |
etāvatsakhi vedmi sāmpratamahaṃ tasyāṅgasaṅge punaḥ
ko'yaṃ kāsmi rataṃ nu vā kathamiti svalpāpi me na smṛtiḥ ||104||(101)
children.translated_text: When the beloved came to the bed, the girdle-knot slipped by itself from its fastening; the garment, loosely held by the girdle strings, remained just barely on the hips. This much, O friend, I know at present — but when it came to the bodily union with him, 'Who is this? Who am I? Was there pleasure or how?' — I have not the slightest memory. // 104 // (101)

children.text:
prāsāde sā diśi diśi ca sā pṛṣṭhataḥ sā puraḥ sā
paryaṅke sā pathi pathi ca sā tadviyogāturasya |
haṃho cetaḥ prakṛtiraparā nāsti me kāpi sā sā
sā sā sā sā jagati sakale ko'yamadvaitavādaḥ ||105||(102)
children.translated_text: She is in the palace, she is in every direction, she is behind, she is in front, she is on the couch, she is on every path — for one afflicted by separation from her. Alas, O mind, there is no other nature for me — she, she, she, she, she, she, she, she throughout the whole world — what is this doctrine of non-duality? // 105 // (102)

children.text:
anālocya premṇaḥ pariṇatimanādṛtya suhṛdas
tvayākāṇḍe mānaḥ kimiti sarale preyasi kṛtaḥ |
samākṛṣṭā hyete virahadahanodbhāsuraśikhāḥ
svahastenāṅgārāstad alamadhunāraṇyaruditaiḥ ||112 (?)|| (80)
children.translated_text: Without considering the consequences of love, disregarding friends, why, O guileless beloved, have you taken up this untimely pride? For these blazing flames of the fire of separation have been drawn forth by your own hand as burning coals — enough now with weeping in the wilderness! // 112(?) // (80)
(<s>Subhāṣitāvalī</s> 1170; <s>Saduktikarṇāmṛta</s> 2.42.1, <s>Sūktimuktāvalī</s> 56.9, <s>Subhāṣitaratnakoṣa</s> 659)

children.text: Verses found in Arjunavarmadeva's version not found here
children.translated_text: Verses found in <s>Arjunavarmadeva</s>'s version not found here.

children.text: aṅgulyagranakhena bāṣpasalilaṃ vikṣipya vikṣipya kiṃ
children.translated_text: Flicking away tear-drops again and again with the tip of the finger-nail, why

children.text: tūṣṇīṃ rodiṣi kopane bahutaraṃ phūtkṛtya rodiṣyasi |
children.translated_text: Do you weep silently? If angry, you will weep even more with loud sobs.

children.text: yasyāste piśunopadeśavacanairmāne'tibhūmiṃ gate
children.translated_text: She whose pride has gone to its extreme through the words and counsel of slanderers —

children.text: nirviṇṇo'nunayaṃ prati priyatamo madhyasthatāmeṣyate ||(5)
children.translated_text: Her dearest, wearied of making amends, will resort to indifference. // (5) //

children.text: tadvaktrābhimukhaṃ mukhaṃ vinamitaṃ dṛṣṭiḥ kṛtā pādayos
children.translated_text: The face was turned toward his face, then bent down; the gaze was fixed upon his feet;

children.text: tasyālāpakutūhalākulatare śrotre niruddhe mayā |
children.translated_text: My ears, exceedingly agitated by curiosity about his words, were blocked by me;

children.text: pāṇibhyāṃ ca tiraskṛtaḥ sapulakaḥ svedodgamo gaṇḍayoḥ
children.translated_text: With my hands I pushed away [his touch], yet there were goosebumps, and sweat broke out on my cheeks —

children.text: sakhyaḥ kiṃ karavāṇi yānti śatadhā yatkañcuke sandhayaḥ ||(11)
children.translated_text: O friends, what shall I do? The fastenings of my bodice are splitting in a hundred ways! // (11) //

children.text: nāpeto'nunayena yaḥ priyasuhṛdvākyairna yaḥ saṃhṛto
children.translated_text: That [pride] which was not removed by entreaty, which was not dissolved by the words of dear friends,

children.text: yo dīrghaṃ divasaṃ viṣahya viṣamaṃ yatnātkathaṃciddhṛtaḥ |
children.translated_text: Which was painfully endured through the long day, somehow maintained with effort —

children.text: anyonyasya hṛte mukhe nihitayostiryakkathaṃciddṛśoḥ
children.translated_text: When the faces of the two were brought close to each other, and sidelong glances were somehow exchanged,

children.text: sa dvābhyāmativismṛtavyatikaro māno vihasyojjhitaḥ ||(42)
children.translated_text: That pride, its quarrel completely forgotten by both, was abandoned with laughter. // (42) //

children.text: rātrau vāribharālasāmbudaravodvignena jātāśruṇā
children.translated_text: At night, by a traveler alarmed by the sound of clouds heavy with rain, his tears flowing,

children.text: pānthenātmaviyogaduḥkhapiśunaṃ gītaṃ tathotkaṇṭhayā |
children.translated_text: A song was sung with longing, betraying the sorrow of separation from his own [beloved];

children.text: āstāṃ jīvitahāriṇaḥ pravasanālāpasya saṃkīrtanaṃ
children.translated_text: Let alone the recounting of the speech of departure that takes away life —

children.text: mānasyāpi jalāñjaliḥ sarabhasaṃ lokena datto yathā ||(54)
children.translated_text: Even to pride, a water-offering [in farewell] was hastily given by the people [who heard it]. // (54) //

children.text: capalahṛdayae kiṃ svātantryāttathā gṛhamāgataś
children.translated_text: O fickle-hearted one, why of your own accord did you come home thus?

children.text: caraṇapatitaḥ premārdrārdraḥ priyaḥ samupekṣitaḥ |
children.translated_text: The beloved, fallen at your feet, tender with love, was ignored.

children.text: tadidamadhunā yāvajjīvaṃ nirastasukhodayā
children.translated_text: Now, for the rest of your life, with the arising of joy destroyed,

children.text: ruditaśaraṇā durjātānāṃ sahasva ruṣāṃ phalam ||(56)
children.translated_text: Taking refuge in tears — endure the fruit of your ill-fated anger! // (56) //

children.text: āstāṃ viśvasanaṃ sakhīṣu viditābhiprāyasāre jane
children.translated_text: Let alone confiding in friends — among people whose intentions are transparent,

children.text: tatrāpyarpayituṃ dṛśaṃ suracitāṃ śaknomi na vrīḍayā |
children.translated_text: Even there I cannot direct my carefully composed gaze, out of shame.

children.text: loko'pyeṣa paropahāsacaturaḥ sūkṣmeṅgitajño'pyalaṃ
children.translated_text: This world too is skilled in mocking others, quite capable of reading subtle gestures —

children.text: mātaḥ kaṃ śaraṇaṃ vrajāmi hṛdaye jīrṇo'nurāgānalaḥ ||(63)
children.translated_text: O mother, to whom shall I take refuge? The fire of love has consumed my heart. // (63) //

children.text: analpacintābharamohaniścalā vilokyamānaiva karoti sādhvasam |
children.translated_text: Motionless with the weight of no small care, she causes alarm even when merely looked upon;

children.text: svabhāvaśobhānatimātrabhūṣaṇā tanustaveyaṃ bata kiṃ nu sundari ||(65)
children.translated_text: Adorned by nothing more than her natural beauty — is this slender body [really] yours, O beautiful one? // (65) //

children.text: iti priye pṛcchati mānavihvalā kathaṃcidantardhṛtabāṣpagadgadam |
children.translated_text: When the beloved thus asked, she, bewildered by pride, somehow with tears suppressed and voice choked,

children.text: na kiṃcidityeva jagāda yadvadhūḥ kiyanna tenaiva tayāsya varṇitam ||(66)
children.translated_text: Said only 'It is nothing' — yet by that alone, how much was not described by the bride to him! // (66) //
