children.text:
jyākṛṣṭibaddhakhaṭakāmukhapāṇipṛṣṭha-
preṅkhannakhāṃśucayasaṃvalito'mbikāyāḥ |
tvāṃ pātu mañjaritapallavakarṇapūra-
lobhabhramadbhramaravibhramabhṛtkaṭākṣaḥ ||1||(1)
children.translated_text: May the sidelong glance of <s>Ambikā</s> protect you — accompanied by the cluster of rays from her nails glinting on the back of her hand, [her hand] held in a fist-like grip [as if] drawing the bowstring, [her glance] bearing the playful movement of bees hovering in desire for the ear-ornament of blossoming tender shoots. // 1 // (1)
(<s>Subhāṣitaratnakoṣa</s> 100, <s>Saduktikarṇāmṛta</s> 123)

children.text:
kṣipto hastāvalagnaḥ prasabhamabhihato'pyādadānoṃśukāntaṃ
gṛhṇan keśeṣvapāstaścaraṇanipatito nekṣitaḥ sambhrameṇa |
āliṅgan yo'vadhūtastripurayuvatibhiḥ sāśrunetrotpalābhiḥ
kāmīvārdrāparādhaḥ sa dahatu duritaṃ śāmbhavo vaḥ śarāgniḥ ||2||(2)
children.translated_text: Thrown off when clinging to the hand, struck forcefully yet still grasping the edge of the garment, seizing the hair yet pushed away, falling at the feet yet not looked upon in [her] agitation — he who, while embracing, was cast aside by the women of the Triple City with tear-filled lotus-eyes — may that fire of <s>Śambhu</s>'s arrow, like a lover guilty of a tender offense, burn away your sins. // 2 // (2)

children.text: (harabāṇaḥ; su. 49, sad. 76)
children.translated_text: (<s>Harabāṇa</s>, i.e., <s>Śiva</s>'s arrow; <s>Subhāṣitaratnakoṣa</s> 49, <s>Saduktikarṇāmṛta</s> 76)

children.text:
ālolāmalakāvalīṃ vilulitāṃ bibhraccalatkuṇḍalaṃ
kiñcinmṛṣṭaviśeṣakaṃ tanutaraiḥ khedāmbhasāṃ śīkaraiḥ |
tanvyā yatsuratāntatāntanayanaṃ vaktraṃ rativyatyaye
tattvāṃ pātu cirāya kiṃ hariharabrahmādibhirdaivataiḥ ||3||(3)
children.translated_text: Bearing her disheveled mass of tossing curls, with swaying earrings, her decorative mark slightly smudged by the fine spray of the waters of exertion — the face of the slender woman at the end of lovemaking, with languid, weary eyes, in the reversed love-play — may that protect you forever. What need of <s>Hari</s>, <s>Hara</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and other gods? (3)

children.text: (viparītaratam- sad. 1141, śā. 3702)
children.translated_text: (Reversed love-play; <s>Saduktikarṇāmṛta</s> 1141, <s>Śārṅgadharapaddhati</s> 3702)

children.text:
alasavalitaiḥ premārdrārdrairmuhurmukulīkṛtaiḥ
kṣaṇamabhimukhairlajjālolairnimeṣaparāṅmukhaiḥ |
hṛdayanihitaṃ bhāvākūtaṃ vamadbhirivekṣaṇaiḥ
kathaya sukṛtī ko'yaṃ mugdhe tvayādya vilokyate ||4||(4)
children.translated_text: With glances languidly turning, drenched and tender with love, now and again half-closing, for a moment meeting directly, then bashfully rolling, then turning away in a blink — as if pouring out the heart's secret emotion — tell me, O innocent one, what fortunate man do you gaze upon today? (4)

children.text: (vāsakasajjā; su. 508; sad. 658)
children.translated_text: (The woman prepared for her lover's visit; <s>Subhāṣitāvalī</s> 508; <s>Saduktikarṇāmṛta</s> 658)

children.text:
datto'syāḥ praṇayastvayaiva bhavatā ceyaṃ ciraṃ lālitā
daivād adya kila tvameva kṛtavān asyā navaṃ vipriyam |
manyurduḥsaha eṣa yātyupaśamaṃ no sāntvavādaiḥ sphuṭaṃ
he nistraṃśa vimuktakaṇṭhakaruṇaṃ tāvatsakhī roditu ||5||(6)
children.translated_text: 'It was you yourself who gave her your love; it was you who long cherished her; by fate's decree, it is you yourself who have now done her a fresh injury. This unbearable anger does not subside with soothing words. O heartless one — let her friend at least weep aloud, releasing her throat!' (5)

children.text:
likhannāste bhūmiṃ bahiravanataḥ prāṇadayito
nirāhārāḥ skahyaḥ satataruditocchūṇanayanāḥ |
parityaktaṃ sarvaṃ hasitapaṭhitaṃ pañjaraśukais
tavāvasthā ceyaṃ visṛja kaṭhine mānamadhunā ||6||(7)
children.translated_text: 'Your life's-beloved sits outside, head bowed, scratching the ground; your friends are without food, eyes swollen from constant weeping; everything is abandoned; even the parrot in its cage has stopped its laughter and recitation — and this is your condition! O hard-hearted one, give up your jealous pride now!' (6)

children.text: (sakhīprabodhaḥ; sad. 713, rasārṇavasudhākara 2.206a)
children.translated_text: (The friend's admonition; <s>Saduktikarṇāmṛta</s> 713, <s>Rasārṇavasudhākara</s> 2.206a)

children.text:
nāryastanvi haṭhāddharanti ramaṇaṃ tiṣṭhanti no vāritās
tatkiṃ tāmyasi kiṃ ca rodiṣi mudhā tāsāṃ priyaṃ mā kṛthāḥ |
kāntaḥ keliruciryuvā sahṛdayastādṛkpatiḥ kātarae
kiṃ no barkarakarkaraiḥ priyaśatairākramya vikrīyate ||7||(8)
children.translated_text: 'Women, O slender one, forcibly steal a lover and do not stop when restrained — so why do you despair? Why do you weep in vain? Do not do as they please! Your husband is amorous, loves play, is young, warm-hearted — such a husband, O timid one — is he not to be seized and bargained for with hundreds of dear rivals crowding in?' (7)

children.text:
\footnote{motīlāla-banārsīdāsa-sampādane (1983):
nāryo mugdhaśaṭhā haranti ramaṇaṃ tiṣṭhanti no vāritās
children.translated_text: [Footnote: In the Motīlāla-Banārasīdāsa edition (1983): 'Women, both innocent and cunning, steal a lover and do not stop when restrained...']

children.text:
kopātkomalalolabāhulatikāpāśena baddhā dṛḍhaṃ
nītvā keliniketanaṃ dayitayā sāyaṃ sakhīnāṃ puraḥ |
bhūyo'pyevamiti skhalan mṛdugirā saṃsūcya duśceṣṭitaṃ
dhanyo hanyata eva nihnutiparaḥ preyān rudatyā hasan ||8||(9)
children.translated_text: Firmly bound with the vine-creeper of her soft and swaying arms in anger, dragged in the evening before her friends to the bower of sport by the beloved — then, stumbling again with soft words, indicating his misbehavior thus — blessed is the beloved who is beaten by his laughing, weeping mistress even as he denies all! (8)

children.text: (śaṭhanāyakaḥ, sad. 882, sū. 85.3, subh. 1351)
children.translated_text: (The deceitful hero; <s>Saduktikarṇāmṛta</s> 882, <s>Sūktimuktāvalī</s> 85.3, <s>Subhāṣitāvali</s> 1351)

children.text:
praharaviratau madhye vāhnastato'pi pare'thavā
kimuta sakale jāte vāhnipriya tvamihaiṣyasi |
iti dinaśataprāpyaṃ deśaṃ priyasya yiyāsato
harati gamanaṃ bālālāpaiḥ sabāṣpagalajjalaiḥ ||9||(12)
children.translated_text: 'After one <s>prahara</s> (three hours)? In the middle of the day? Or even after that? Or perhaps when the whole day has passed — beloved, will you come here then?' — Thus with childish words mingled with streaming tears, the young woman arrests the departure of her beloved who is setting out for a land requiring a hundred days' [journey]. (9)

children.text: (prasthānabhaṅgaḥ - su. 532, sad. 921, subh. 1048, śā. 3389, sū. 37.7)
children.translated_text: (Interruption of departure; <s>Subhāṣitāvalī</s> 532, <s>Saduktikarṇāmṛta</s> 921, <s>Subhāṣitāvali</s> 1048, <s>Śārṅgadharapaddhati</s> 3389, <s>Sūktimuktāvalī</s> 37.7)

children.text:
yātāḥ kiṃ na milanti sundari punaścintā tvayā matkṛte
no kāryā nitarāṃ kṛśāmi kathayatyevaṃ sabāṣpe mayi |
lajjāmantharatārakeṇa nipataddhārāśruṇā cakṣuṣā
dṛṣṭvā māṃ hāsitena bhāvimaraṇotsāhastayā sūcitaḥ ||10||(10)
children.translated_text: 'Those who have gone — do they not return, O beautiful one? Do not worry on my account — I am not so much wasting away' — thus I said, with tears. But seeing me, with eyes from which tears streamed down, the stars of shyness moving slowly — with that smile, she indicated her readiness for death. (10)

children.text:
dhīraṃ vāridharasya vāri kirataḥ śrutvā niśīthe dhvaniṃ
dīrghocchvāsamudaśruṇā virahiṇīṃ bālāṃ ciraṃ dhyāyatā |
adhvanyena vimuktakaṇṭhamakhilāṃ rātriṃ tathā kranditaṃ
grāmīṇairvrajato janasya vasatirgrāme niṣiddhā yathā ||11||(13)
children.translated_text: Hearing at midnight the sound of the cloud pouring rain steadily, the woman in separation, with long sighs and tears, brooding long over the young beloved — [the traveler] on the road wept the entire night, his throat released, so that the village folk forbade him lodging in the village as he passed. (11)

children.text: (varṣāpathikaḥ, sad. 915)
children.translated_text: (The traveler in the rains; <s>Saduktikarṇāmṛta</s> 915)

children.text:
kathamapi sakhi krīḍākopād vrajeti mayodite
kaṭhinahṛdayastyaktvā śayyāṃ balād gata eva saḥ |
iti sarabhasaṃ dhvastapremṇi vyapetaghṛṇe jane
punarapi hatavrīḍaṃ cetaḥ prayāti karomi kim ||12||(15)
children.translated_text: 'When I said in playful anger 'Go!', the hard-hearted one actually left the bed and went by force' — thus, when the one whose love was shattered and whose compassion had departed was gone, her shameless mind goes after him once more — 'What am I to do?' (12)

children.text:
dampatyorniśi jalpatorgṛhaśukenākarṇitaṃ yadvacas
tatprātargurusannidhau nigadatastasyopahāraṃ vadhūḥ |
karṇālaṅkṛtipadmarāgaśakalaṃ vinyasya cañcūpuṭe
vrīḍārtā prakaroti dāḍimaphalavyājena vāgbandhanam ||13||(16)
children.translated_text: What the couple spoke to each other in the night was overheard by the household parrot; when it repeated those words the next morning in the presence of the elders, the bride, stricken with embarrassment, placed a piece of ruby from her ear-ornament in its beak, and under the pretense of [giving it] a pomegranate seed, silenced it. (13)

children.text: (śukoktivrīḍā, kuval. 173, su. 621, sad. 1180, subh. 2214, śā. 3743)
children.translated_text: (Embarrassment caused by the parrot's speech; <s>Kuvalayānanda</s> 173, <s>Subhāṣitāvalī</s> 621, <s>Saduktikarṇāmṛta</s> 1180, <s>Subhāṣitāvali</s> 2214, <s>Śārṅgadharapaddhati</s> 3743)

children.text:
ajñānena parāṅmukhīṃ paribhavād āśliṣya māṃ duḥkhitāṃ
kiṃ labdhaṃ caṭula tvayeha nayatā saubhāgyametāṃ daśām |
paśyaitad dayitākucavyatikaron mṛṣṭāṅgarāgāruṇaṃ
vakṣaste malatailapaṅkaśavalairveṇīpadairaṅkitam ||14||(17)
children.translated_text: 'By embracing me in ignorance when my face was turned away, and in distress from your insult — what have you gained, O fickle one, by bringing your good fortune to this state? Look — your chest, reddened by the sandalwood-paste rubbed from the breasts of your mistress, is now marked with the mud-stains of hair-oil and the traces of her braids.' (14)

children.text: (khaṇḍitā)
children.translated_text: (The woman betrayed; <s>khaṇḍitā</s>)

children.text:
ekatrāsanasaṃsthitiḥ parihatā pratudgamād dūratas
tāmbūlānayanacchalena rabhasāśelṣo'pi saṃvighnitaḥ |
ālāpo'pi na miśritaḥ parijanaṃ vyāpārayantyāntike
kāntaṃ pratyupacārataścaturayā kopaḥ kṛtārthīkṛtaḥ ||15|| (18)
children.translated_text: Sitting together in one seat was rejected; the greeting from afar was blocked; even a sudden embrace, under the pretext of fetching betel, was thwarted. Conversation too was avoided by keeping servants busy nearby. The clever woman, through formal courtesies, brought her anger to fruition against her beloved. (15)

children.text: (māninī, sad. 692, rasārṇavasudhākara 2.67g)
children.translated_text: (The sulking woman; <s>Saduktikarṇāmṛta</s> 692, <s>Rasārṇavasudhākara</s> 2.67g)

children.text:
dṛṣṭvaikāsanasaṃsthite priyatame paścād upetyādarād
ekasyā nayane pidyāya vihitakrīḍānubandhacchalaḥ |
īṣadvakrimakandharaḥ sapulakaḥ premollasanmānasām
antarhāsalasatkapolaphalakāṃ dhūrto'parāṃ cumbati ||16||(19)
children.translated_text: Seeing his beloveds seated together, approaching from behind with affection, covering the eyes of one under the pretense of initiating a game — with neck slightly bent, with goosebumps, while the other, her heart blossoming with love, with cheek radiant with a hidden smile — the rogue kisses the other one. (16)

children.text: (śaṭhanāyakaḥ, su. 603, sad. 881)
children.translated_text: (The deceitful hero; <s>Subhāṣitāvalī</s> 603, <s>Saduktikarṇāmṛta</s> 881)

children.text:
caraṇapatanapratyākhyānātprasādaparāṅmukhe
nibhṛtakitavācāretyuktvā ruṣā puruṣīkṛte |
vrajati ramaṇe niḥśvasyoccaiḥ stanasthitahastayā
nayanasalilacchannā dṛṣṭiḥ sakhīṣu niveśitā ||17||(20)
children.translated_text: When her beloved departed, his prostration at her feet rejected, her favors refused — after she cried out in anger 'Villain of secret treachery!' and he, now the man, walked away — sighing deeply, with hands on her breasts, her gaze veiled with tears, she fixed her eyes upon her friends. (17)

children.text: (mānināyakaḥ, sad. 896)
children.translated_text: (The hero who maintains his pride; <s>Saduktikarṇāmṛta</s> 896)

children.text:
kāñcyā gāḍhatarāvaruddhavasanaprāntā kimarthaṃ punar
mugdhākṣī svaiptīti tatparijanaṃ svairaṃ priye pṛcchati |
mātaḥ svaptumapīha vārayati māmityāhitakrodhayā
paryasya svapiticchalena śayane datto'vakāśastayā ||18||(21)
children.translated_text: 'Why does the doe-eyed one sleep with the hem of her garment tightly bound by her girdle?' — when the beloved freely asks her attendants — 'Mother! He won't even let me sleep here!' — [saying this] with feigned anger, she turns on the bed and, under the pretense of sleeping, gives him an opening. (18)

children.text: (śayanādhirohanam, sad. 1094, subh. 2081, sū. 77.11)
children.translated_text: (Ascending the bed; <s>Saduktikarṇāmṛta</s> 1094, <s>Subhāṣitāvali</s> 2081, <s>Sūktimuktāvalī</s> 77.11)

children.text:
ekasmiñśayane parāṅmukhatayā vītottaraṃ tāmyator
anyonyasya hṛdi sthite'pyanunaye saṃrakṣatorgauravam |
dampatyoḥ śanakairapāṅgavalanān miśrībhavaccakṣuṣor
bhagno mānakaliḥ sahāsarabhasaṃ vyāsaktakaṇṭhagraham ||19||(23)
children.translated_text: On the same bed, turned away from each other, both suffering without reply, though reconciliation was in each other's hearts, both preserving their dignity — of the couple, from slow sidelong turns, as their gazes gradually merged, the quarrel of pride was broken — swiftly, with laughter, in a sudden embrace of each other's necks. (19)

children.text: (mānabhaṅgaḥ, sad. 723)
children.translated_text: (The breaking of pride; <s>Saduktikarṇāmṛta</s> 723)

children.text:
paśyāmo mayi kiṃ prapadyata iti sthairyaṃ mayālambitaṃ
kiṃ māmālapatītyayaṃ khala śaṭhaḥ kopastayāpyāśritaḥ |
ityanyonyavilakṣadṛṣṭicature tasminnavasthāntare
savyājaṃ hasitaṃ mayā dhṛtiharo bāṣpastu muktastayā ||20||(24)
children.translated_text: 'Let us see what befalls me' — thus I adopted firmness. 'Will he address me?' — that villain, that rogue — thus she too resorted to anger. And in that state, both casting embarrassed sidelong glances at each other, skillfully — a feigned laugh was given by me, stealing her composure; but tears were released by her. (20)

children.text: (uccāvacaṃ, kuval., 185; sad. 1366)
children.translated_text: (The fluctuations; <s>Kuvalayānanda</s> 185; <s>Saduktikarṇāmṛta</s> 1366)

children.text:
parimlāne māne mukhaśaśini tasyāḥ karadhṛte
mayi kṣīṇopāye praṇipatanamātraikaśaraṇe |
tayā pakṣmaprāntavrajapuṭaniruddhena sahasā
prasādo bāṣpena stanataṭaviśīrṇena kathitaḥ ||21||(25)
children.translated_text: When her pride had withered, the moon-face held in her hands, and I, exhausted of all stratagems, had only prostration as my last refuge — by her, with tears suddenly checked in the enclosure of her eyelash-tips, then spilling over the slope of her breasts — her favor was declared. (21)

children.text: (uccāvacaṃ, sad. 1367, subh. 1608, sū. 58.1)
children.translated_text: (The fluctuations; <s>Saduktikarṇāmṛta</s> 1367, <s>Subhāṣitāvali</s> 1608, <s>Sūktimuktāvalī</s> 58.1)

children.text:
tasyāḥ sāndravilepanastanataṭapraśleṣamudrāṅkitaṃ
kiṃ vakṣaścaraṇānativyatikaravyājena gopāyyate |
ityukte kva tad ityudīrya sahasā tatsampramārṣṭuṃ mayā
sāśliṣṭā rabhasena tatsukhavaśāttanvyāpi tad vismṛtam ||22||(26)
children.translated_text: 'Is that chest — bearing the seal-imprint of her breasts pressed close in thick unguent — being hidden under the pretense of a prostration at my feet?' — When this was said, I exclaimed 'Where is it?' and in hastily trying to wipe it away, I embraced the slender woman tightly — and in the pleasure of that, even she forgot [the offense]. (22)

children.text:
tvaṃ mugdhākṣi vinaiva kañculikayā dhatse manohāriṇīṃ
lakṣmīmityabhidhāyini priyatame tadvīṭikāṃ saṃspṛśi |
śayyopāntaniviṣṭasasmitamukhīnetrotsavānandito
niryātaḥ śanakairalīkavacanopanyāsamālījanaḥ ||23||(27)
children.translated_text: 'O doe-eyed one, even without your bodice you bear enchanting beauty' — when the beloved says this and touches her betel-case, the servant-woman, seated at the bedside with a smiling face, delighted by the festival of her mistress's eyes, slowly departed — skilled in the pretext of false words. (23)

children.text:
bhrūbhaṅge racite'pi dṛṣṭiradhikaṃ sotkaṇṭhamudvīkṣate
kārkaśyaṃ gamite'pi cetasi tanūromāñcamālambate |
ruddhāyāmapi vāci sasmitamidaṃ dagdhānanaṃ jāyate
dṛṣṭe nirvahaṇaṃ bhaviṣyati kathaṃ mānasya tasmiñjane ||24||(28)
children.translated_text: Though the brow-knitting was composed, the gaze looks out with even greater longing; though hardness was maintained in the heart, the body takes on a thrill of goosebumps; though speech was restrained, this smiling blush spreads over the face — when that person is seen, how can the maintenance of jealous pride succeed? (24)

children.text: (anuraktamāninī, su. 695, sad. 702, subh. 1580; uṇ. 5.25)
kānte katyapi vāsarāṇi gamaya tvaṃ mīlayitvā dṛśau
children.translated_text: 'Beloved, pass some days with eyes closed;'

children.text: svasti svasti nimīlayāmi nayane yāvan na śūnyā diśaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Be well, be well — I close my eyes, so long as the directions are not empty [of you].'

children.text: āyātā vayamāgamiṣyati suhṛdvargasya bhāgyodayaiḥ
children.translated_text: 'We have come; the circle of friends shall come, by the rising of fortune.'

children.text: sandeśo vada kastavābhilaṣitastīrtheṣu toyāñjaliḥ ||25||
children.translated_text: 'Tell me, what is your wish? A water-offering at the sacred fords?' (25)
(The loving woman in jealous anger; <s>Subhāṣitāvalī</s> 695, <s>Saduktikarṇāmṛta</s> 702, <s>Subhāṣitāvali</s> 1580; <s>Uṇādisūtra</s> 5.25)

children.text: (yātrākṣepaḥ, sad.731 (vīrasya))
children.translated_text: (Interruption of the journey; <s>Saduktikarṇāmṛta</s> 731 [of the hero])

children.text:
sā patyuḥ prathamāparādhasamaye sakhyopadeśaṃ vinā
no jānāti savibhramāṅgavalanāvakroktisaṃsūcanam |
svacchairacchakapolamūlagalitaiḥ paryastanetrotpalā
bālā kevalameva roditi luṭhallolālakairaśrubhiḥ ||26||(29)
children.translated_text: She, at the time of her husband's first offense, without a friend's instruction, does not know the art of indicating [displeasure] through coquettish bodily turns, sidelong words, and suggestions. The young woman, with blue-lotus eyes upturned, with clear tears streaming down from the base of her clear cheeks — she simply weeps, with stray curls tossing with her tears. (26)

children.text: (mugdhā; sad.498)
children.translated_text: (The innocent woman; <s>Saduktikarṇāmṛta</s> 498)

children.text:
bhavatu viditaṃ chadmālāpairalaṃ priya gamyatāṃ
tanurapi na te doṣo'smākaṃ vidhistu parāṅmukhaḥ |
tava yathā tathābhūtaṃ prema prapannamimāṃ daśāṃ
prakṛticapale kā naḥ pīḍā gate hatajīvite ||27||(30)
children.translated_text: 'Let it be understood; enough of deceitful sweet-talk; go, O beloved — the fault is not yours, nor even of this slender body; it is fate that is averse. Your love, however it may be, has come to this state — O fickle one by nature, what grief is ours when life itself is gone?' // 27 // (30)

children.text: (māninīvākyam; sad. 708; pad. 223)
children.translated_text: (Speech of a proud woman [<s>māninī</s>]; <s>Saduktikarṇāmṛta</s> 708; <s>Padyāvalī</s> 223)

children.text:
urasi nihitastāro hāraḥ kṛtā jaghane ghane
kalakalavatī kāñcī pādau kvaṇanmaṇinūpurau |
priyamabhisarasyevaṃ mugdhe samāhataḍiṇḍimā
yadi kimadhikatrāsotkampaṃ diśaḥ samudīkṣase ||28||(31)
children.translated_text: A glittering pearl necklace is placed upon the breast, a tinkling girdle on the heavy hips, jingling jeweled anklets on the feet — O naive one, you go to meet your lover thus, with drums beating as it were; if so, why do you look about in every direction, trembling with excessive fear? // 28 // (31)

children.text:
prātaḥ prātarupāgatena janitā nirnidritā cakṣuṣor
mandāyāṃ mayi gauravavyapagamād utpāditaṃ lāghavam |
kiṃ mugdhe na mayā kṛtaṃ ramaṇadhīrmuktā tvayā gamyatāṃ
dusthaṃ tiṣṭhasi yacca pathyamadhunā kartāsmi tacchroṣyasi ||29||(33)
children.translated_text: 'You have caused sleeplessness in my eyes by coming every morning; when I was slow [to respond], your lack of respect produced a sense of triviality in me — what have I not done, O naive one?' The husband's resolve was released by her — 'Go! You stand uncomfortably here — what is wholesome [for you] now, I shall do — you will hear of it.' // 29 // (33)

children.text:
sā bālā vayamapragalbhamanasaḥ sā strī vayaṃ kātarāḥ
sā pīnonnatimatpayodharayugaṃ dhatte sakhedā vayam |
sākrāntā jaghanasthalena guruṇā gantuṃ na śaktā vayaṃ
doṣairanyajanāśritairapaṭavo jātāḥ sma ityadbhutam ||30||(34)
children.translated_text: She is young, and we are timid of heart; she is a woman, and we are cowards; she bears a pair of breasts full and uplifted, and we are troubled; she is weighed down by her heavy hips and cannot walk, and we — we have become incapable due to faults belonging to another person. How astonishing! // 30 // (34)

children.text: (anukūlanāyakaḥ, su. 481, sad. 872, subh. 1346, s.k. 3.42)
children.translated_text: (The well-disposed hero [<s>anukūla-nāyaka</s>]; <s>Subhāṣitaratnakoṣa</s> 481, <s>Saduktikarṇāmṛta</s> 872, <s>Subhāṣitāvalī</s> 1346, <s>Sūktimuktāvalī</s> 3.42)

children.text:
prasthānaṃ valayaiḥ kṛtaṃ priyasakhairajasraṃ gataṃ
dhṛtyā na kṣaṇamāsitaṃ vyavasitaṃ cittena gantuṃ puraḥ |
gantuṃ niścitacetasi priyatame sarve samaṃ prasthitā
gantavye sati jīvitapriyasuhṛtsārthaḥ kimu tyajyate ||31||(35)
children.translated_text: The bangles have declared their departure [by falling], dear friends have incessantly departed, fortitude has not sat [with me] even for a moment, the mind has resolved to go ahead — when the dearest one has decided to go, all have set forth together. When one must go, why should the caravan of life's dear friends be abandoned? // 31 // (35)

children.text: (proṣitabhartṛkāvacanam; subh. 1151; śā. 3424; sad. 741; sū. 37.19)
children.translated_text: (Speech of a woman whose husband is away [<s>proṣita-bhartṛkā</s>]; <s>Subhāṣitāvalī</s> 1151; <s>Śārṅgadharapaddhati</s> 3424; <s>Saduktikarṇāmṛta</s> 741; <s>Sūktimuktāvalī</s> 37.19)

children.text:
sandaṣṭādharapallavā sacakitaṃ hastāgramādhunvatī
māmāmuñca śaṭheti kopavacanairānartitabhrūlatā |
śītkārāñcitalocanā sarabhasaṃ yaiścumbitā māninī
prāptaṃ tairamṛtaṃ mudhaiva mathito mūḍhaiḥ suraiḥ sāgaraḥ ||32||(36)
children.translated_text: Biting her tender lower lip, tremblingly waving the tips of her fingers, with eyebrows dancing in anger at the words 'Let me go, you deceitful one!' — the proud woman who was kissed thus by those [lovers] has obtained nectar; in vain was the ocean churned by the foolish gods! // 32 // (36)

children.text: (cumbanam, sad. 1105, subh. 1303, śā. 3668)
children.translated_text: (On kissing; <s>Saduktikarṇāmṛta</s> 1105, <s>Subhāṣitāvalī</s> 1303, <s>Śārṅgadharapaddhati</s> 3668)

children.text:
supto'yaṃ sakhi supyatāmiti gatāḥ sakhyastato'nantaraṃ
premāvāsitayā mayā saralayā nyastaṃ mukhaṃ tanmukhe |
jñāte'līkanimīlane nayanayordhūrtasya romāñcito
lajjāsīn mama tena sāpyapahṛtā tatkālayogyaiḥ kramaiḥ ||33||(37)
children.translated_text: 'He is asleep, O friend — let us sleep too,' said my friends and departed. Then I, artless and perfumed with love, placed my face upon his face. When the feigned closing of the rogue's eyes was discovered, I was overcome with shame — and that too was stolen by him through means appropriate to the moment. // 33 // (37)

children.text:
kopo yatra bhrūkuṭiracanā nigraho yatra maunaṃ
yatrānyonyasmitamanunayo yatra dṛṣṭiḥ prasādaḥ |
tasya premṇastad idamadhunā vaiṣamaṃ paśya jātaṃ
tvaṃ pādānte luṭhasi nahi me manyumokṣaḥ khalāyāḥ ||34||(38)
children.translated_text: Where anger means the knitting of brows, where restraint means silence, where a mutual smile serves as reconciliation, and where a glance is the mark of favor — see now what difficulty has arisen in that love of ours: you grovel at my feet, yet there is no release of my anger, wicked woman that I am! // 34 // (38)

children.text: (nāyake māninī, sad. 709)
children.translated_text: (The proud woman [<s>māninī</s>] toward the hero; <s>Saduktikarṇāmṛta</s> 709)

children.text:
sutanu jahihi kopaṃ paśya pādānataṃ māṃ
na khalu tava kadācitkopa evaṃ vidho'bhūt |
iti nigadati nāthe tiryagāmīlitākṣyā
nayanajalamanalpaṃ muktamuktaṃ na kiñcit ||35||(39)
children.translated_text: 'O slender one, abandon your anger — look, I bow at your feet; truly your anger has never been of this kind before!' As the lord spoke thus, with eyes half-closed and turned aside, she shed copious tears — yet uttered not a word. // 35 // (39)

children.text: (mānabhaṅgaḥ, sad. 725)
children.translated_text: (The breaking of pride [<s>māna-bhaṅga</s>]; <s>Saduktikarṇāmṛta</s> 725)

children.text:
gāḍhāliṅganavāmanīkṛtakucaprodbhinnaromodgamā
sāndrasneharasātirekavigalatśrīmannitambāmbarā |
mā mā mānada māti māmalamiti kṣāmākṣarollāpinī
suptā kiṃ nu mṛtā nu kiṃ manasi me līnā vilīnā nu kim ||36||(40)
children.translated_text: Her breasts pressed flat by a tight embrace, goosebumps risen, the garment on her beautiful hips slipping from the excess of intense love — murmuring with languid eyes 'No, no, O giver of honor, stop, enough, stop!' — is she asleep, or dead, or absorbed in my mind, or dissolved? // 36 // (40)

children.text:
paṭālagne patyau namayati mukhaṃ jātavinayā
haṭhāśleṣaṃ vāñchatyapaharati gātrāṇi nibhṛtam |
na śaknotyākhyātuṃ smitamukhasakhīdattanayanā
hriyā tāmyatyantaḥ prathamaparihāse navavadhūḥ ||37||(41)
children.translated_text: When her husband touches her garment's edge, the new bride modestly lowers her face; she desires a forceful embrace yet quietly withdraws her limbs; she cannot speak, her eyes given to a smiling friend — inwardly she is overcome with shame at the first teasing of the new bride. // 37 // (41)

children.text: (navoḍhā; sad. 512, subh. 2056, śā. 3673; viṣṇudās u.ṇ. 5.19)
children.translated_text: (The new bride [<s>navoḍhā</s>]; <s>Saduktikarṇāmṛta</s> 512, <s>Subhāṣitāvalī</s> 2056, <s>Śārṅgadharapaddhati</s> 3673; <s>Viṣṇudās</s> <s>Uṇādisūtra</s> 5.19)

children.text:
gate premābandhe praṇayabahumāne vigalite
nivṛtte sadbhāve jana iva jane gacchati puraḥ |
tad utprekṣyotprekṣya priyasakhi gatāṃstāṃśca divasān
na jāne ko heturdalati śatadhā yan na hṛdayam ||38||(43)
children.translated_text: When the bond of love has gone, when affectionate regard has faded, when good faith has departed, and he passes before me like any stranger among strangers — reflecting upon those departed days again and again, O dear friend, I do not know what reason there is that the heart does not split into a hundred pieces. // 38 // (43)

children.text: (uccāvacaṃ, su. 697, sad. 1368, subh. 1141, śā. 3545, sū. 84.1, rasārṇavasudhākara 2.263c)
children.translated_text: (<s>Uccāvaca</s> [mixed feelings]; <s>Subhāṣitaratnakoṣa</s> 697, <s>Saduktikarṇāmṛta</s> 1368, <s>Subhāṣitāvalī</s> 1141, <s>Śārṅgadharapaddhati</s> 3545, <s>Sūktimuktāvalī</s> 84.1, <s>Rasārṇavasudhākara</s> 2.263c)

children.text:
ciravirahiṇorutkaṇṭhārtiślathīkṛtagātrayor
navamiva jagaj jātaṃ bhūyaścirād abhinandatoḥ |
kathamapi dine dīrghe yāte niśāmadhirūḍhayoḥ
prasarati kathā bahvī yūnoryathā na tathā ratiḥ ||39||(44)
children.translated_text: For the two long-separated ones, their limbs loosened by the anguish of longing, rejoicing after a long time as if the world were created anew — when somehow the long day has passed and they have ascended to the night, much conversation flows between the young couple, but not so much lovemaking. // 39 // (44)

children.text:
dīrghā vandanamālikā viracitā hṛṣṭyaiva nendīvaraiḥ
puṣpāṇāṃ prakaraḥ smitena racito no kundajātyādibhiḥ |
dattaḥ svedamucā payodharayuge nārghyo na kumbhāmbhasā
svairevāvayavaiḥ priyasya viśatastanvyā kṛtaṃ maṅgalam ||40||(45)
children.translated_text: The long garland of salutation was fashioned by joy alone, not by blue lotuses; the heap of flowers was made by smiles, not by <s>kunda</s> and jasmine blossoms; the <s>arghya</s> (offering) was given by the sweat-releasing pair of breasts, not by water from a pitcher — with her own body-parts the slender woman performed the auspicious welcome for her entering beloved. // 40 // (45)

children.text:
kānte sāgasi śāyite priyasakhīveśaṃ vidhāyāgate
bhrāntyāliṅgya mayā rahasyamuditaṃ tatsaṅgamākāṅkṣayā |
mugdhe duṣkarametad ityatitarāmuktvā sahāsaṃ balād
āliṅgya chalitāsmi tena kitavenādya pradoṣāgame ||41||(46)
children.translated_text: When my guilty beloved was lying [in bed], I came disguised as her dear friend, and in secret she embraced me in confusion, out of her desire for his union — 'O naive one, this is difficult!' said she, and saying this with a laugh, she forcefully embraced [me]; I was tricked by that deceitful woman at the onset of dusk tonight! // 41 // (46)

children.text:
āśaṅkya praṇatiṃ paṭāntapihitau pādau karotyādarāt
vyājenāgatamāvṛṇoti hasitaṃ na spaṣṭamudvīkṣate |
mayyālāpavati pratīpavacanaṃ sakhyā sahābhāṣate
tasyāstiṣṭhatu nirbharapraṇayitā māno'pi ramyodayaḥ ||42||(47)
children.translated_text: She respectfully covers her feet with the edge of her garment, suspecting a prostration; she conceals the smile that has arisen with a pretext; she does not look directly; when I speak, she addresses contrary words to her friend — let her generous affection stand; even her pride has a charming dawn. // 42 // (47)
(<s>Subhāṣitāvalī</s> 1590, <s>Śārṅgadharapaddhati</s> 3537, <s>Sūktimuktāvalī</s> 55.11)

children.text:
sā yāvanti padānyalīkavacanairālījanaiḥ śikṣitā
tāvantyeva kṛtāgaso drutataraṃ vyāhṛtya patyuḥ puraḥ |
prārabdhā purato yathā manasijasyājñā tathā vartituṃ
premṇo maugdhyavibhūṣaṇasya sahajaḥ ko'pyeṣa kāntaḥ kramaḥ ||43||(48)
children.translated_text: As many words as the friends had taught her through false speeches, just that many she uttered rapidly before her guilty husband — then she began to act before him as the commands of <s>Kāma</s> (the Love God) dictated. This is some innate and charming way of love, whose ornament is naivety. // 43 // (48)

children.text:
dūrādutsukamāgate vivalitaṃ sambhāṣiṇi sphāritaṃ
saṃśliṣyatyaruṇaṃ gṛhītavasane kiñcin natabhrūlatam |
māninyāścaraṇānativyatikare bāṣpāmbupūrṇekṣaṇaṃ
cakṣurjātamaho prapañcacaturaṃ jātāgasi preyasi ||44||(49)
children.translated_text: When he arrived eagerly from afar, her gaze was averted; when he spoke, it widened; when embracing, it reddened; when he grasped her garment, the brows were slightly knit; when the proud woman fell at his feet in reciprocation, her eyes filled with tears — alas, how artful in its manifestations became the eye, when the beloved was at fault! // 44 // (49)

children.text:
aṅgānāmatitānavaṃ kathamidaṃ kampaśca kasmātkuto
mugdhe pāṇḍukapolamānanamiti prāṇeśvare pṛcchati |
tanvyā sarvamidaṃ svabhāvajamiti vyāhṛtya pakṣmāntara
vyāpī bāṣpabharastayā calitayā niḥśvasya mukto'nyataḥ ||45||(50)
children.translated_text: 'Why this excessive thinness of the limbs? And whence this trembling? O naive one, why the pale cheeks and face?' — when the lord of her life asked thus, the slender woman replied 'All this is natural' and departed, trembling, with a flood of tears spreading between her lashes, having sighed and released [him] to go elsewhere. // 45 // (50)

children.text:
purastanvyā gotraskhalanacakito'haṃ natamukhaḥ
pravṛtto vailakṣyātkimapi likhituṃ daivahatakaḥ |
sphuṭo rekhānyāsaḥ kathamapi sa tādṛk pariṇato
gatā yena vyaktaṃ punaravayavaiḥ saiva taruṇī ||46||(51)
children.translated_text: In her presence, startled by the slip of [uttering another's] name, I lowered my face, and in my embarrassment, accursed by fate, began to draw something or other [on the ground]. The tracing of the lines was clear, but somehow it turned out in such a way that there emerged unmistakably, limb by limb, that very young woman! // 46 // (51)

children.text: \footnote{asya ślokasya parārdhaḥ:
tataścābhijñāya sphuradaruṇagaṇḍasthalarucā
children.translated_text: Then, having recognized [the drawing], with cheeks flushed and radiant,

children.text: manasvinyā rūḍhapraṇayasahasodgadgadagirā |
children.translated_text: With voice choked with emotion born of deep-rooted love, the proud woman [said]:

children.text: aho citraṃ citraṃ sphuṭamiti nigadyāśrukaluṣaṃ
children.translated_text: 'Oh, how strange, how strange! It is manifest!' — and speaking thus, her eyes clouded with tears,

children.text: ruṣā brahmāstraṃ me śarasi nihito vāmacaraṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In anger: 'A <s>brahmāstra</s> (supreme weapon) has been aimed at my heart — your left foot [has been placed upon me]!' //
[Footnote: The second half of this verse:]

children.text: (gotraskhalitam, sad. 686)
children.translated_text: (On the slip of the name [<s>gotraskhalita</s>]; <s>Saduktikarṇāmṛta</s> 686)

children.text:
kaṭhinahṛdaye muñca bhrāntiṃ vyalīkakathāśritāṃ
piśunavacanairdukhaṃ netuṃ na yuktamimaṃ janam |
kimidamathavā satyaṃ mugdhe tvayā hi viniścitaṃ
yad abhirucitaṃ tan me kṛtvā priye sukhamāsyatām ||47||(53)
children.translated_text: 'O hard-hearted one, abandon the delusion founded on false tales; it is not right to bring suffering to this person through the words of slanderers. Or rather, O naive one, if you have truly ascertained this — having done as pleases you, O beloved, may you remain happy.' // 47 // (53)

children.text: mandaṃ mudritapāṃśavaḥ paripatajjhaṅkārajhañjhāmarud
children.translated_text: With softly stirring dust, with the buzzing and roaring monsoon wind

children.text: vegadhvastakuṭīrakāntaragatacchidreṣu labdhāntarāḥ |
children.translated_text: Finding openings in the gaps of huts destroyed by its force,

children.text: karmavyagrakuṭumbinīkucataṭasvedacchidaḥ prāvṛṣaḥ
children.translated_text: Relieving the sweat on the breast-slopes of housewives busy with their tasks —

children.text: prārambhe nipatanti kandaladalollāsāḥ payobindavaḥ ||48||
children.translated_text: At the onset of the rains, water-drops fall, glistening like <s>kandala</s> (wild plantain) leaves. // 48 //

children.text: \footnote{prakṣipto'yaṃ śloka iti arjunavarmadevapādāḥ|
children.translated_text: [Footnote: This verse is considered an interpolation by the revered <s>Arjunavarmadeva</s>.]

children.text: pītastuṣārakiraṇo madhunaiva sārdham
children.translated_text: The moon, consumed together with the wine,

children.text: antaḥ praviśya caṣake pratibimbavartī |
children.translated_text: Having entered within the cup, abides as a reflection;

children.text: mānāndhakāramapi mānavatījanasya
children.translated_text: Surely it shattered even the darkness of pride in the hearts of proud women,

children.text: nūnaṃ bibheda yad asau prasasāda sadyaḥ ||49||
children.translated_text: For she was instantly appeased. // 49 //

children.text:
\footnote{rudramadevakumārasya ṭīkāyāmapyeṣa śloko dṛśyate|
(madhupānam, sad. 1089, subh. 2022, śā. 3648)
children.translated_text: [Footnote: This verse is also found in the commentary of <s>Rudramadeva Kumāra</s>.] (On drinking wine [<s>madhupāna</s>]; <s>Saduktikarṇāmṛta</s> 1089, <s>Subhāṣitāvalī</s> 2022, <s>Śārṅgadharapaddhati</s> 3648)

children.text: nabhasi jaladalakṣmīṃ sambhṛtāṃ vīkṣya diṣṭyā
children.translated_text: Having seen the gathering beauty of rain-clouds in the sky, [she began] 'By good fortune,

children.text: prasarasi yadi kāntetyardhamuktvā kathañcit |
children.translated_text: If you set forth, O beloved —' and having somehow spoken half [the sentence],

children.text: mama paṭamavalambya prollikhantī dharitrīṃ
children.translated_text: Clutching my garment, scratching the earth [with her toe],

children.text: tadanukṛtavatī sā yatra vāco nivṛttāḥ ||50||
children.translated_text: She enacted the rest [of the sentence] where words had ceased. // 50 //

children.text: \footnote{vemabhūpālasya ṭīkāyāmapyeṣa śloko dṛśyate|
children.translated_text: [Footnote: This verse is also found in the commentary of King <s>Vemabhūpāla</s>.]

children.text: iyamasau taralāyatalocanā
children.translated_text: She with the tremulous, wide eyes,

children.text: gurusamunnatapīnapayodharā |
children.translated_text: With breasts heavy, lofty, and full,

children.text: pṛthunitambabharālasagāminī
children.translated_text: Moving languidly with the weight of her broad hips —

children.text: priyatamā mama jīvitahāriṇī ||51||
children.translated_text: My dearest beloved, the stealer of my life. // 51 //

children.text: \footnote{prakṣipto'yaṃ śloka iti arjunavarmadevamahāśayāḥ|
children.translated_text: [Footnote: This verse is considered an interpolation by the revered <s>Arjunavarmadeva</s>.]

children.text: sālaktakena navapallavakomalena
children.translated_text: With a foot soft as a fresh sprout, reddened with <s>ālaktaka</s> (lac-dye),

children.text: pādena nūpuravatā madanālasena |
children.translated_text: adorned with anklets, languid with desire —

children.text: yastāḍyate dayitayā praṇayārādhāt
children.translated_text: he who is kicked by his beloved out of a lover's pique,

children.text: so'ṅgīkṛto bhagavatā makaradhvajena ||52||
children.translated_text: that man is favored by the blessed <s>Makaradhvaja</s> (the god of love). ||52||

children.text:
\footnote{vemabhūpālasya ṭīkāyāmeṣa ślokaḥ kevalaṃ labhyate|
(anukūlanāyakaḥ, sad. 873, sū. 85.1)
children.translated_text:
\footnote{vemabhūpālasya ṭīkāyāmeṣa ślokaḥ kevalaṃ labhyate|
(anukūlanāyakaḥ, sad. 873, sū. 85.1)

children.text:
bāle nātha vimuñca mānini ruṣaṃ roṣān mayā kiṃ kṛtaṃ
khedo'smāsu na me'parādhyati bhavān sarve'parādhā mayi |
tatkiṃ rodiṣi gadgadena vacasā kasyāgrato rudyate
nanvetan mama kā tavāsmi dayitā nāsmītyato rudyate ||53||(57)
children.translated_text: "Dear girl, O lord, give up your sulking, O proud one, your anger — what wrong have I done?" "The grief is ours, I am not at fault." "You are the one who wrongs — all faults are mine." "Then why do you weep?" With a voice choked with sobs: "Before whom shall I weep?" "Why, before me!" "Who am I to you?" "My beloved." "I am not!" "Then why do you weep?" ||53||(57)

children.text: (māninī, sad. 691, subh. 1614)
children.translated_text: (māninī, sad. 691, subh. 1614)

children.text:
nītvoccairvikṣipantaḥ kṛtatuhinakaṇāsārasaṅgān parāgān
kaundān ānanditālīn atitarasurabhīn bhūriśo diṅmukheṣu |
ete te kuṅkumāktastanakalasabharāsphālanād ucchalantaḥ
pītvā śītkārivaktraṃ śiśuharidṛśāṃ haimanā vānti vātāḥ||54||
children.translated_text: Carrying aloft and scattering pollen mixed with frost-drops and hail, from <s>kunda</s> blossoms, delighting the bees, exceedingly fragrant, across all the quarters — these wintry winds blow, stained with saffron from dashing against the pitcher-like fullness of breasts, having drunk from the lips that gasp with cold, of young women with eyes like baby deer. ||54||

children.text: \footnote{rudramadevakumārasya ṭīkāyāmapyeṣa śloko dṛśyate|
children.translated_text: \footnote{rudramadevakumārasya ṭīkāyāmapyeṣa śloko dṛśyate|

children.text: śrutvā tanvyā niśīthe navaghanarasitaṃ viślathāṅkaṃ patitvā
children.translated_text: Hearing at midnight the rumbling of fresh clouds, the slender woman falls upon her bed with limbs gone slack,

children.text: śayyāyāṃ bhūmipṛṣṭhe karataladhṛtayā duḥkhitālījanena |
children.translated_text: upon the bare floor, supported by the hands of her grieving companions —

children.text: sotkaṇṭhaṃ muktakaṇṭhaṃ kaṭhinakucataṭāghātaśīrṇāśrubindu
children.translated_text: with yearning, with throat released in full cry, tears shattered against her firm, hard breasts,

children.text: smṛtvā smṛtvā priyasya skhalitamṛduvaco rudyate pānthabadhvā ||55||
children.translated_text: remembering again and again the tender, faltering words of her beloved, the traveler's wife weeps. ||55||

children.text: \footnote{rudramadevakumārasya ṭīkāyāmeṣa ślokaḥ kevalaṃ dṛśyate|
children.translated_text: \footnote{rudramadevakumārasya ṭīkāyāmeṣa ślokaḥ kevalaṃ labhyate|

children.text:
śliṣṭaḥ kaṇṭhe kimiti na mayā mūḍhayā prāṇanāthaś
cumbatyasmin vadanavidhutiḥ kiṃ kṛtā kiṃ na dṛṣṭaḥ |
noktaḥ kasmād iti navavadhūceṣṭitaṃ cintayantī
paścāttāpaṃ vahati taruṇī premṇi jāte rasajñā ||56||(58)
children.translated_text: "Why did I not embrace my lord around the neck, foolish that I was? When he kissed me, why did I turn my face away? Why did I not gaze at him? Why did I not speak?" — thus pondering the ways of a new bride, the young woman, now awakened to the taste of love, bears the weight of remorse. ||56||(58)

children.text: (uccāvacaḥ, sad. 1369, subh. 2143)
children.translated_text: (uccāvacaḥ, sad. 1369, subh. 2143)

children.text:
śrutvā nāmāpi yasya sphuṭaghanapulakaṃ jāyate'ṅgaṃ samantāt
dṛṣṭvā yasyānanenduṃ bhavati vapuridaṃ candrakāntānukāri |
tasminnāgatya kaṇṭhagrahaṇasarabhasasthāyini prāṇanāthe
bhagnā mānasya cintā bhavati mama pnarvajramayyāḥ kadā nu ||57||(59)
children.translated_text: Merely hearing whose name causes the body to bristle visibly with goosebumps on every side; seeing whose moon-like face, this body becomes like a <s>candrakānta</s> (moonstone, melting at the moon's touch) — when that lord of my life comes and stands clasping my neck in eager embrace, the resolve of my pride shatters. When, oh when, shall my pride become adamantine? ||57||(59)

children.text: rāmāṇāṃ ramaṇīyavaktraśaśinaḥ svedodabindupluto
children.translated_text: The faces of lovely women are moons drenched with drops of perspiration;

children.text: vyālolālakavallarīṃ pracalayan dhunvan nitambāmbaram |
children.translated_text: swaying the restless creeper-like curls, fluttering the garments at their hips —

children.text: prātarvāti madhau prakāmavikasadrājīvarājīrajo
children.translated_text: in spring at dawn, laden with pollen-dust from lavishly blooming blue lotuses,

children.text: jālāmodamanoharo ratirasaglāniṃ haranmārutaḥ ||58||
children.translated_text: enchanting with its web of fragrance, dispelling the weariness of love's pleasure — such is the breeze that blows. ||58||

children.text:
\footnote{rudramadevakumārasya ṭīkāyāmapyeṣa śloko vartate|
(prābhātikavātaḥ; sad. 459)
children.translated_text:
\footnote{rudramadevakumārasya ṭīkāyāmapyeṣa śloko vartate|
(prābhātikavātaḥ; sad. 459)

children.text: aṅgaṃ candanapāṇḍupallavamṛdustāmbūlatāmrādharo
children.translated_text: The body pale as sandal-paste, soft as a tender shoot, the lower lip reddened by <s>tāmbūla</s> (betel),

children.text: dhārāyantrajalābhiṣekakaluṣe dhautāñjane locane |
children.translated_text: the eyes, their collyrium washed away, clouded by the spray of fountain-water,

children.text: antaḥpuṣpasugandhirārdrakavarī sarvāṅgalagnāmbaraṃ
children.translated_text: the hair damp and fragrant with flowers within, garments clinging to every limb —

children.text: romāṇāṃ ramaṇīyatāṃ vidadhati grīṣmāparāhvāgame ||59||
children.translated_text: such is the loveliness that women display at the onset of summer afternoons. ||59||

children.text: \footnote{rudramadevakumārasya ṭīkāyāmapyeṣa śloko dṛśyate|
children.translated_text: \footnote{rudramadevakumārasya ṭīkāyāmapyeṣa śloko dṛśyate|

children.text: varamasau divaso na punarniśā
children.translated_text: Better that day should perish, and not the night;

children.text: nanu niśaiva varaṃ na punardivā |
children.translated_text: nay, let the night alone perish, not the day!

children.text: ubhayametad upaitvathavā kṣayaṃ
children.translated_text: Or rather, let both day and night come to an end —

children.text: priyajanena na yatra samāgamaḥ ||60||
children.translated_text: wherever there is no reunion with the beloved. ||60||

children.text: \footnote{rudramadevakumārasya ṭīkāyāmeṣa ślokaḥ kevalaṃ labhyate|
children.translated_text: \footnote{rudramadevakumārasya ṭīkāyāmeṣa ślokaḥ kevalaṃ labhyate|

children.text:
lolairlocanavāribhiḥ saśapathaiḥ pādapraṇāmaiḥ priyair
anyāstā vinivārayanti kṛpaṇāḥ prāṇeśvaraṃ prasthitam |
puṇyāhaṃ vraja maṅgalaṃ sudivasaṃ prātaḥ prayātasya te
yatsnehocitamīhitaṃ priyatama tvaṃ nirgataḥ śroṣyasi ||61||(61)
children.translated_text: Some women restrain their departing lord with unsteady tears and earnest oaths and cherished prostrations at his feet. But one says: "Go with blessings! May there be good fortune! An auspicious day! You who set forth at dawn — what tenderness befits our love, O dearest, you shall hear of it once you have gone." ||61||(61)

children.text: (yātrākṣepaḥ, sad. 735, s.v. 1060, śā. 3395, sū. 37.12)
children.translated_text: (yātrākṣepaḥ, sad. 735, s.v. 1060, śā. 3395, sū. 37.12)

children.text:
lagnā nāṃśukapallave bhujalatā na dvāradeśe'pitā
no vā pādatale tayā nipatitaṃ tiṣṭheti noktaṃ vacaḥ |
kāle kevalamambudātimaline gantuṃ pravṛttaḥ śaṭhaḥ
tanvyā bāṣpajalaughakalpitanadīpūreṇa baddhaḥ priyaḥ ||62||(62)
children.translated_text: Her vine-like arms did not cling to the hem of his garment; she did not stand blocking the doorway; nor did she fall at his feet; nor did she utter the word "Stay!" — yet when the rogue set out to leave under a sky dark with heavy clouds, the beloved was held fast by the flood of a river formed from the torrent of the slender woman's tears. ||62||(62)

children.text: (prasthānabhaṅgaḥ, sad. 922, subh. 1057, śā. 3388, sū. 37.5)
children.translated_text: (prasthānabhaṅgaḥ, sad. 922, subh. 1057, śā. 3388, sū. 37.5)

children.text:
na jāne saṃmukhāyāte priyāṇi vadati priye |
sarvāṇyaṅgāni me yānti śrotratāṃ kimu netratām ||63||(64)
children.translated_text: I do not understand — when my beloved comes before me and speaks sweet words, all my limbs seem to become ears; what then to say of becoming eyes? ||63||(64)

children.text: (nāyikābhilāṣaḥ, sad. 960)
children.translated_text: (nāyikābhilāṣaḥ, sad. 960)

children.text:
virahaviṣamaḥ kāmo vāmastanuṃ kurute tanuṃ
divasagaṇanād akṣaścāsau vyapetaghṛṇo yamaḥ |
tvamapi vaśago mānavyādhervicintaya nātha he
kiśalayamṛdurjīved evaṃ kathaṃ pramadājanaḥ ||64||(67)
children.translated_text: <s>Kāma</s> (desire), cruel in separation, makes the body ever more wasted; counting the days, that merciless one is <s>Yama</s> (Death) himself with his dice; you too are in the power of the hunter of pride — consider this, O lord! How shall a woman, tender as a young shoot, survive thus? ||64||(67)

children.text: (mānināyakaḥ; sad. 898, subh. 1633, śā. 3572)
children.translated_text: (mānināyakaḥ; sad. 898, subh. 1633, śā. 3572)

children.text:
pādāsakte suciramiha te vāmatā kaiva kānte
sanmārgasthe praṇayini jane kopane ko'parādhaḥ |
itthaṃ tasyāḥ parjanakathā kopavegopaśāntau
bāṣpodbhedaistad anu sahasā na sthitaṃ na prayātam ||65||(68)
children.translated_text: "You cling so long at my feet — what is this perverseness, O beloved? When a loving heart treads the right path, what offense warrants anger?" — thus, as her fury subsided through talk of other matters, tears suddenly broke forth; and she neither stayed nor departed. ||65||(68)

children.text:
purābhūdasmākaṃ niyatamavibhinnā tanuriyaṃ
tato nu tvaṃ preyānvayamapi hatāśāḥ priyatamāḥ |
idānīṃ nāthastvaṃ vayamapi kalatraṃ kimaparaṃ
mayāptaṃ prāṇānāṃ kuliśakaṭhinānāṃ phalamidam ||66||(69)
children.translated_text: "Once our bodies were inseparably one; then you became the lover, and I the hapless beloved; now you are 'lord' and I mere 'wife' — what more is there to say? This is the fruit I have won — of my diamond-hard resolve to live." ||66||(69)

children.text:
mugdhe mudghatayaiva netumakhilaḥ kālaḥ kimārabhyate
mānaṃ dhatsva dhṛtiṃ vadhāna ṛjutāṃ dūre kuru preyasi |
sakhyaivaṃ pratibodhitā prativacastāmāha bhītānanā
nīceḥ śaṃsa hṛdi sthito nanu sa me prāṇeśvaraḥ śroṣyati ||67||(70)
children.translated_text: "Foolish girl, should all of time be spent in sulking alone? Hold to your pride, strengthen your resolve, cast off your yielding, keep your lover at a distance!" — thus counseled by her friend, the girl replied with frightened face: "Hush! Speak softly — my lord dwells within my heart. Surely he will hear!" ||67||(70)

children.text: pīto yataḥ prabhṛti kāmapipāsitena
children.translated_text: Ever since the nectar of that dear one's lips was drunk

children.text: tasyā mayādhararasaḥ pracuraḥ priyāyāḥ |
children.translated_text: by me, thirsting with the thirst of <s>Kāma</s> (desire), in abundance —

children.text: tṛṣṇā tataḥ prabhṛti me dviguṇatvameti
children.translated_text: from that moment my craving has doubled in force;

children.text: tāvaṇyamasti bahu tatra kimapi citram ||68||
children.translated_text: such is the wonder of her beauty — what marvel is there in this? ||68||

children.text: \footnote{prakṣipto'yaṃ śloka iti arjunavarmadevamahāśayāḥ|
children.translated_text: \footnote{prakṣipto'yaṃ śloka iti arjunavarmadevamahāśayāḥ|

children.text:
kva prasthitāsi karabhoru ghane niśīthe
prāṇādhiko vasati yatra janaḥ priyo me |
ekākinī vada kathaṃ na bibheṣi bāle
nanvasti puṅkhitaśaro madanaḥ sahāyaḥ ||69||(71)
children.translated_text: "Where do you go, O fair-thighed one, in the thick of night?" "Where the one dearer than life to me dwells." "Alone — tell me, are you not afraid, child?" "Is not <s>Madana</s> (the god of love), his arrow fitted to the string, my companion?" ||69||(71)

children.text:
līlāttāmarasāhato'nyavanitāniḥśaṅkadaṣṭādharaḥ
kaścitkesaradūṣitekṣaṇa iva vyāmīlya netre sthitaḥ |
mugdhā kudmalitānanena dadhato vāyuṃ sthitā tasya sā
bhrāntyā dhūrtatayā ca vepathumatī tenāniśaṃ cumbitā ||70||(72)
children.translated_text: A certain man, struck playfully with a lotus by another woman, his lower lip bitten by her without shame, his eyes as if smeared with pollen, stood with eyes half-closed. His innocent beloved stood fanning him with her face turned away — and he, whether from trembling at her nearness or from sheer cunning, kissed her ceaselessly. ||70||(72)

children.text:
sphuṭatu hṛdayaṃ kāmaṃ kāmaṃ karatu tanuṃ tanuṃ
na sakhi caṭulapremṇā kāryaṃ punardayitena me |
iti sarabhasaṃ mānāṭopād udīrya vacastayā
ramaṇapadavī sāraṅgākṣyā saśaṅkitamīkṣitā ||71||(73)
children.translated_text: "Let my heart burst if it will! Let <s>Kāma</s> (desire) make my body waste away! I shall have nothing more to do with my fickle-hearted lover, O friend!" — having uttered these impetuous words in the vehemence of her pride, the doe-eyed girl then cast an anxious glance along the path her lover might take. ||71||(73)

children.text: (anuraktamāninī; su. 666, sad. 705, sū. 55.1)
children.translated_text: (anuraktamāninī; su. 666, sad. 705, sū. 55.1)

children.text:
gāḍhāśleṣaviśīrṇacandanarajaḥpuñjaprakarṣādiyaṃ
śayyā samprati komalāṅgi paruṣetyāropya māṃ vakṣasi |
gāḍhauṣṭhagrahapūrvamākulatayā pādāgrasaṃdaṃśake-
nākṛṣyāmbaramātmano yaducitaṃ dhūrtena tatprastutam ||72||(74)
children.translated_text: "The sandal-paste is scattered by our tight embrace and the bed has become rough now, O soft-limbed one" — saying this, the rogue drew her upon his chest, and with a deep kiss upon her lips, in seeming confusion, with his toes he pulled away her own garment — thus did the cunning one arrange what he desired. ||72||(74)

children.text:
kathamapi kṛtapratyākhyāne priye skhalitottare
virahakṛśayā kṛtvā vyājaṃ prakalpitamaśrutaṃ |
asahanasakhīśrotraprāptipramādasasaṃbhramaṃ
vigalitadṛśā śūnye gehe samucchvasitaṃ punaḥ ||73||(75)
children.translated_text: When the beloved's entreaty was somehow refused, and his halting reply had come, the woman, wasted by separation, contrived a pretext — a fabricated, unheard-of tale — delivered with the feigned alarm and flustered urgency of something unbearable reaching a friend's ear; and then, with dissolving gaze, in the empty house, she breathed deeply once more. ||73||(75)

children.text:
ādṛṣṭiprasarātpriyasya padavīmudvīkṣya nirviṇṇayā
vicchinneṣu pathiṣvahaḥpariṇatau dhvānte samutsarpati |
dattaikaṃ saśucā gṛhaṃ prati padaṃ pānthastriyāsminkṣaṇe
mā bhūdāgata ityamandavalitagrīvaṃ punarvīkṣitam ||74||(76)
children.translated_text: Having gazed as far as sight could reach along the path of her beloved, now despairing, as the roads were lost from view and the day declined and darkness crept forward — the traveler's wife, placing one grief-laden step toward home, at that very moment thought: "What if he has come!" — and with neck eagerly turned, she looked back once more. ||74||(76)

children.text:
āyāte dayite manorathaśatairnītvā kathaṃciddinaṃ
vaidagdhyāpagamājjaḍe parijane dīrghāṃ kathāṃ kurvati |
daṣṭāsmītyabhidhāya satvarapadaṃ vyādhūya cīnāṃśukaṃ
tanvaṅgyā ratikātareṇa manasā nītaḥ pradīpaḥ śamam ||75||(77)
children.translated_text: When the beloved arrived, after somehow enduring the day with a hundred daydreams, and the attendants — their sophistication now fled — stood dull-wittedly prolonging a tedious conversation, she cried, "I've been bitten!" and with hasty steps, shaking off her silken <s>cīnāṃśuka</s> (Chinese silk garment), with a mind impatient for love's pleasure, the slender-limbed woman extinguished the lamp. ||75||(77)

children.text:
ālambyāṅgaṇavāṭikāparisare cūtadrume mañjarīṃ
sarpatsāndraparāgalampaṭaraṭadbhṛṅgāṅganāśobhinīm |
manye svāṃ tanumuttarīyaśakalenācchādya bālā sphurat-
kaṇṭhadhvānanirodhakampitakucaśvāsodgamā roditi ||76||(78)
children.translated_text: Clutching at a mango bough in the courtyard garden's edge — a cluster of blossoms made beautiful by swarming, wanton bees drunk on thick-spreading pollen — the young girl, I imagine, covers her body with the edge of her upper cloth, and with voice breaking in her throat, her breasts heaving with suppressed sobs, her breath rising in gasps, she weeps. ||76||(78)

children.text:
yāsyāmiti samudyatasya gaditaṃ visrabdhamākarṇitaṃ
gacchandūramupekṣito muhurasau vyāvṛtya tiṣṭhannapi |
tacchūnye punarāsthitāsmi bhavane prāṇāsta ete dṛḍhāḥ
sakhyastiṣṭhata jīvitavyasaninī dambhādahaṃ rodimi ||77||(79)
children.translated_text: "He will go" — when he made ready to depart, his words were heard with composure; as he walked further away, he was ignored, though he turned back again and again and lingered. But now — in this empty house I sit once more; these wretched lives of mine are obstinate indeed. Friends, stand by me: I, clinging shamelessly to life, weep only out of pretense. ||77||(79)

children.text:
śūnyaṃ vāsagṛhaṃ vilokya śayanādutthāya kiṃcicchanair
nidrāvyājamupāgatasya suciraṃ nirvarṇya patyurmukham ||
children.translated_text: Seeing the bedchamber empty, rising slowly from the bed,

children.text:
visrabdhaṃ paricumbya jātapulakāmālokya gaṇḍastalīṃ
lajjānamramukhī priyeṇa hasatā bālā ciraṃ cumbitā ||78||(82)
children.translated_text: Having gazed long at the face of her husband who had come feigning sleep — having kissed him boldly, then seeing the goosebumps on his cheek, the young woman with face lowered in shame was kissed long by her laughing beloved. // 78 // (82)

children.text:
loladbhrūlatayā vipakṣadigupanyāse'vadhūtaṃ śiras
tadvṛttāntanirīkṣaṇe kṛtanamaskāro vilakṣaḥ sthitaḥ |
kopāttāmrakapolabhittini mukhe dṛṣṭyā gataḥ pādayor
utsṛṣṭo gurusannidhāvapi vidhirdvābhyāṃ na kālocitaḥ ||79||(83)
children.translated_text: By the moving eyebrow-vine, when the glance was cast toward the rival's direction, the head was shaken [in disapproval]; upon witnessing that incident, [the lover] stood embarrassed, having offered a bow. In anger, upon the cheek-wall flushed copper, the gaze fell to [her] feet — [yet even] in the presence of elders, [propriety] was abandoned; the conduct of neither of the two was timely. // 79 // (83)

children.text:
jātā notkalikā stanau na lulitau gātraṃ na romāñcitaṃ
vaktraṃ svedakaṇānvita na sahasā yāvacchaṭhenāmunā |
dṛṣṭenāva mano hṛtaṃ dhṛtimuṣā prāṇeśvareṇādya me
tatkenātra nirūpyamāṇanipuṇo mānaḥ samādhīyatām ||80||(84)
children.translated_text: No excitement arose, the breasts were not caressed, the body was not thrilled with goosebumps, the face was not suddenly covered with beads of sweat — yet by this rogue, merely by being seen, my mind was stolen today by the lord of my life who robs resolve. Now by what [means] shall a pride skilled in careful assessment be established? // 80 // (84)

children.text:
dṛṣṭaḥ kātaranetrayā cirtaraṃ baddhāñjaliṃ yācit
paścādaṃśukapallavena vidhṛto nirvyājamāliṅgitaḥ |
ityākṣipya yadā samastamaghṛṇo gantuṃ pravṛttaḥ śaṭhaḥ
pūrvaṃ prāṇaparigraho dayitayā muktastato vallabhaḥ ||81||(85)
(Skm 726, Spd 3386, Smv 37.6)
children.translated_text: Looked upon with timid eyes for a long time, entreated with folded hands, then held back by the edge of her garment, embraced without pretense — when, having rejected all of this, the merciless rogue turned to leave, she first released her life-breath, then [released] her beloved. // 81 // (85) (<s>Sūktimuktāvalī</s> 726, <s>Śārṅgadharapaddhati</s> 3386, <s>Sūktimuktāvalī</s> 37.6)

children.text:
kṛto dūrādeva smitamadhuramabhyudgamavidhiḥ
śirasyājñā nyastā prativacanavatyānatimati |
na dṛṣṭeḥ śaithilyaṃ milana iti ceto dahati me
nigūḍhāntaḥkopātkaṭhiṇahṛdaye saṃvṛtiriyam ||82||(14)
children.translated_text: From afar, the protocol of rising to greet was performed with a sweet smile; an authoritative command was placed upon the head along with a reply and a bow. There is no loosening of the gaze at the meeting — this burns my heart: from the proud woman of hard heart whose inner anger is concealed, this is composure! // 82 // (14)

children.text:
ekasmiñśayane vipakṣaramaṇīnāmagrahe mugdhayā
sadyaḥ kopaparāṅmukhaṃ śayitayā cāṭūni kurvannapi |
āvegādavadhīritaḥ priyatamastūṣṇīṃ sthitastatkṣaṇāt
mā bhūssupta ivaiṣa mandavalitagrīvaṃ punarvīkṣitaḥ ||83||(22)
children.translated_text: On one bed, when the naive woman, having heard the name of the rival, immediately lay down turning away in anger — though the beloved made sweet entreaties, he was rejected in her agitation; he remained silent from that moment. 'Lest he be asleep!' — and turning her neck slightly, she looked at him again. // 83 // (22)

children.text:
malayamarutāṃ vrātā yātā vikāsitamallikā
parimalabharo bhagno grīṣmastvamutsahase yadi |
ghana ghaṭayituṃ nisnehaṃ tvāṃ ya eva nivartane
prabhavati gavāṃ kinnaśchinnaṃ sa eva dhanañjayaḥ ||84||(32)
children.translated_text: 'The hosts of Malaya breezes have gone, the blossoming jasmine's fragrance is spent, summer is over — if you desire to set forth, O cloud, the same <s>Dhanañjaya</s> (<s>Arjuna</s>, i.e., the fire) who is able to make you, who are without moisture, turn back, is also able to split you.' // 84 // (32)

children.text:
svaṃ dṛṣṭvā karajakṣataṃ madhumadakṣīvā vicāryerṣyayā
gacchantī kva nu gacchasīti vidhṛtā bālā paṭānte mayā |
pratyāvṛttamukhī sabāṣpanayanā māṃ muñca muñceti sā
kopātprasphuritādharā yadavadattatkena vismaryate ||85||(55)
children.translated_text: Seeing the scratch-marks of her own nails [on his body], intoxicated by wine, pondering with jealousy, the young woman was going [away] — held by me at the edge of her garment [I asked] 'Where are you going?' With face turned back, eyes filled with tears, [she said] 'Let me go, let me go!' — her lip quivering with anger, what she then said — by whom can that be forgotten? // 85 // (55)

children.text: sālaktakaṃ śatadalādhikakāntiramyaṃ
children.translated_text: Adorned with lac-dye, lovelier than a hundred petals,

children.text: ratnaughadhāmanikarāruṇanūpuraṃ ca |
children.translated_text: With anklets reddened by the radiance of clustered gems —

children.text: kṣiptaṃ bhṛśaṃ kupitayā taralotpalākṣyā
children.translated_text: The foot, placed by the angry, tremulous-lotus-eyed woman,

children.text: saubhāgyacihnamiva mūrdhni padaṃ vireje ||86||
children.translated_text: Shone on [his] head like a mark of good fortune. // 86 //

children.text: \footnote{prakṣipto'yaṃ śloka iti arjunavarmadevamahāśayāḥ|
children.translated_text: [Footnote: This verse is considered an interpolation by the revered <s>Arjunavarmadeva</s>.]

children.text:
kapole patrālī karatalanirodhena mṛditā
nipīto niḥśvāsairayamamṛtahṛdyo'dhararasaḥ |
muhuḥ kaṇṭhe lagnastaralayati bāṣpaḥ stanataṭaṃ
priyo manyurjātastava niranurodhe na tu vayam ||87||(81)
children.translated_text: The leaf-pattern on the cheek was smudged by the pressure of the palm; this nectar-sweet flavor of the lip, dear to the heart, was drunk up by sighs; tears clinging again and again to the throat make the breast-slopes tremble — O beloved, your anger has arisen against one who has no regard [for you], but not against us. // 87 // (81)

children.text: (anunayaḥ, su. 664, sad. 720, s.k.v. 489, subh. 1627)
children.translated_text: (Entreaty [<s>anunaya</s>]; <s>Subhāṣitaratnakoṣa</s> 664, <s>Saduktikarṇāmṛta</s> 720, <s>Sūktimuktāvalī</s> 489, <s>Subhāṣitāvalī</s> 1627)

children.text:
lākṣālakṣmalalāṭapaṭṭamabhitaḥ keyūramudrā gale
vaktre kajjalakālimā nayanayorstāmbūlarāgo ghanaḥ |
dṛṣṭā kopavidhāyi maṇḍanamidaṃ prātaściraṃ preyaso
līlātāmarasodare mṛgadṛśaḥ śvāsāḥ samāptiṃ gatāḥ ||88||(60)
(anyaraticihnaduḥkhitā; sad. 594; śā. 3740, subh. 2215; sū. 82.17; pad. 222; daśarūpaka 2.6)
children.translated_text: The lac-mark on the forehead-plate all around, the imprint of armlets on the neck, the blackness of collyrium on the face, the dense stain of betel on the eyes — having seen this anger-provoking ornamentation of the beloved early in the morning for a long time, [reflected] in the playful lotus [of her] belly, the sighs of the doe-eyed woman came to an end. // 88 // (60) (A woman distressed by signs of another's lovemaking; <s>Saduktikarṇāmṛta</s> 594; <s>Śārṅgadharapaddhati</s> 3740, <s>Subhāṣitāvalī</s> 2215; <s>Sūktimuktāvalī</s> 82.17; <s>Padyāvalī</s> 222; <s>Daśarūpaka</s> 2.6)

children.text:
tapte mahāvirahavahniśikhāvalībhir
āpāṇḍurastanataṭe hṛdaye priyāyāḥ |
rathyālivīkṣaṇaniveśitaloladṛṣṭer
nūnaṃ chanacchaniti bāṣpakaṇāḥ patanti ||89||(86)
children.translated_text: In the heart of the beloved, scorched by the flames of the great fire of separation, pale on the breast-slopes — for her who has fixed her wandering gaze on the view of the street, surely the teardrops fall, secretly, drop by drop. // 89 // (86)

children.text:
cintāmohaviniścalena manasā maunena pādānataḥ
pratyākhyānaparāṅmukhaḥ priyatamo gantuṃ pravṛtto'dhunā |
savrīḍairalasairnirantaraluṭhadbāṣpākulairlocanaiḥ
śvāsotkampakucaṃ nirīkṣya suciraṃ jīvāśayā vāritaḥ ||90||(87)
children.translated_text: With mind motionless from anxious brooding, silent, fallen at [her] feet, turning away from reconciliation, the dearest one is now about to depart. With eyes bashful, languid, constantly rolling with tears in agitation, having gazed long at the breasts heaving with sighs — he was restrained by the hope of life. // 90 // (87)

children.text:
tanvaṅgyā gurusannidhau nayanajaṃ yad vāri saṃstambhitaṃ
tenāntargalitena manmathaśikhī sikto'nuṣaṅgodbhavaḥ |
manye tasya nirasyamānakiraṇasyaiṣā mukhenodgatā
śvāsāmodasamākulālinikaravyājena dhūmāvaliḥ ||91||(96)
children.translated_text: The tear-water born from the eyes of the slender-limbed woman was suppressed in the presence of elders — by that [water], flowing inwardly, the fire of <s>Manmatha</s> (the Love God), born of attachment, was doused. I believe this trail of smoke has issued from her mouth, from that [fire] whose flames are being extinguished — in the guise of a swarm of bees stirred by the fragrance of sighs. // 91 // (96)

children.text:
bhrūbhedo racitaḥ ciraṃ nayanayorabhyastamāmīlanaṃ
roddhuṃ śikṣitamādareṇa hasitaṃ maune'bhiyogaḥ kṛtaḥ |
dhairyaṃ kartumapi sthirīkṛtamidaṃ cetaḥ kathañcin mayā
baddho mānaparigrahe parikaraḥ siddhistu daivasthitā ||92||(97)
children.translated_text: The frowning of the brows was practiced, the closing of the eyes was rehearsed long, the laughter was carefully taught to be restrained, an effort at silence was made — somehow this heart was steadied by me to maintain resolve; the girding for the undertaking of pride was bound — but success rests with fate! // 92 // (97)

children.text: \footnote{rūpagosvāmipādasya padyāvalyām (231) etasya ślokasyaiṣa rūpaḥ:
children.translated_text: [Footnote: In the <s>Padyāvalī</s> (231) of the revered <s>Rūpa Gosvāmin</s>, this verse appears in this form:]

children.text: bhrūbhaṅgo guṇitaściraṃ nayanayorabhyastamāmīlanaṃ
children.translated_text: The furrowing of the brows was multiplied, the closing of the eyes was rehearsed long,

children.text: roddhuṃ śikṣitamādareṇa hasitaṃ maune'bhiyogaḥ kṛtaḥ |
children.translated_text: The laughter was carefully taught to be restrained, an effort at silence was made;

children.text: dhairyaṃ kartumapi sthirīkṛtamidaṃ cetaḥ kathañcin mayā
children.translated_text: Somehow this heart was steadied by me to maintain resolve —

children.text: baddho mānaparigrahe parikaraḥ siddhistu daive sthitā ||
children.translated_text: The girding for the undertaking of pride was bound, but success rests with fate! //

children.text: (anuraktamāninī, su. 645, sad. 703, pad. 231)
children.translated_text: (The loving proud woman [<s>anurakta-māninī</s>]; <s>Subhāṣitaratnakoṣa</s> 645, <s>Saduktikarṇāmṛta</s> 703, <s>Padyāvalī</s> 231)

children.text:
deśairantaritā śataiśca saritāmurvībhṛtāṃ kānanair
yatnenāpi na yāti locanapathaṃ kānteti jānannapi |
udgrīvaścaraṇārdharuddhavasudhaḥ kṛtvāśrupūrṇāṃ dṛśaṃ
tāmāśāṃ pathikastathāpi kimapi dhyāyaṃściraṃ vīkṣate ||93||(99)
children.translated_text: Separated by lands, by hundreds of rivers, mountains, and forests, even with effort the beloved does not enter the path of the eyes — knowing this, yet with neck craned, feet half-blocking the earth, having made his gaze brimming with tears, the traveler gazes long at that direction, lost in some thought. // 93 // (99)

children.text: (proṣitaḥ, su. 765, sad. 901, śā. 3445)
children.translated_text: (The man abroad [<s>proṣita</s>]; <s>Subhāṣitaratnakoṣa</s> 765, <s>Saduktikarṇāmṛta</s> 901, <s>Śārṅgadharapaddhati</s> 3445)

children.text:
mlānaṃ pāṇḍu kṛśaṃ viyogavidhuraṃ lambālakaṃ sālasaṃ
bhūyastatkṣaṇajātakānti rabhasaprāpte mayi proṣite |
sāṭopaṃ ratikelikālasarasaṃ ramyaṃ kimapyādarād
yatpītaṃ sutanormayā vadanakaṃ vaktuṃ na tatpāryate ||94||(88)
children.translated_text: Withered, pale, emaciated, wretched from separation, with drooping locks, languid — yet immediately regaining its radiance the moment I, the long-absent one, arrived — the face of the slender woman which I drank in with eager reverence, at once proud and yet languid with the ease of love's play, exquisitely beautiful — that cannot be described. // 94 // (88)

children.text:
saivāhaṃ pramadā nṛṇāmadhigatāvetau ca tau nūpurāv
eṣāsmākamavṛttireva sahajavrīḍādhanaḥ strījanaḥ |
itthaṃ lajjitayā smṛterupagame matvā tanuṃ sambhramāt
pumbhāvaḥ prathamaṃ rativyatikare muktastato vallabhaḥ ||95||(89)
children.translated_text: 'I am that same woman attainable by men, and these are those same anklets; we women are by nature thus — with modesty as our only wealth.' In this way, when the memory arose and she became bashful, he thought [her embarrassment genuine] and in his eagerness, the male state first dissolved during the act of love — then [she embraced] her beloved. // 95 // (89)

children.text:
karakisalayaṃ dhūtvā dhūtvā vimārgati vāsasī
kṣipati sumanomālāśeṣaṃ pradīpaśikhāṃ prati |
sthagayati muhuḥ patyurnetre vihasya samākulā
surataviratā ramyā tanvī muhurmuhurīkṣate ||96||(90)
children.translated_text: Shaking and shaking the tender sprout-like hand, she searches for her garments; she flings the remaining flower garland toward the lamp's flame; she repeatedly covers her husband's eyes, laughing and flustered — the lovely slender woman, having finished lovemaking, gazes again and again. // 96 // (90)

children.text:
santyevātra gṛhe gṛhe yuvatayastāḥ pṛccha gatvādhunā
preyāṃsaḥ praṇamanti kiṃ tava punardāso yathā vartate |
ātmadrohiṇi durjanaiḥ pralapitaṃ karṇe'niśaṃ mā kṛthāś
chinnasneharasā bhavanti puruṣā duḥkhānuvartyāḥ punaḥ ||97||(91)
children.translated_text: 'There are indeed young women in every house — go and ask them now: do the lovers bow down to you as your servant does?' O self-harming one, do not heed what malicious people constantly whisper in your ear — men whose affection has dried up become indifferent; but they follow suffering [back to love]. // 97 // (91)

children.text:
niḥśvāsā vadanaṃ dahanti hṛdayaṃ nirmūlamunmathyate
nidrā neti na dṛśyate priyamukhaṃ rātrindivaṃ rudyate |
aṅgaṃ śoṣamupaiti pādapatitaḥ preyāṃstathopekṣitaḥ
sakhyaḥ kaṃ guṇamākalayya dayite mānaṃ vayaṃ kāritāḥ ||98||(92)
children.translated_text: Sighs burn the face, the heart is uprooted and churned, sleep does not come, the face of the beloved is not seen, day and night there is weeping, the body wastes away, the beloved has fallen at my feet yet is ignored — O friends, having calculated what merit [accrues], for what reason have we been made to maintain our pride toward the beloved? // 98 // (92)

children.text: (pad. 237, sad. 677; daśarūpaka 2.26)
children.translated_text: (<s>Padyāvalī</s> 237, <s>Saduktikarṇāmṛta</s> 677; <s>Daśarūpaka</s> 2.26)

children.text:
adyārabhya yadi priye punarahaṃ mānasya vā'nyasya vā
gṛhṇīyāṃ śaṭhadurnayena manasā nāmāpi saṃkṣepataḥ |
tattenaiva vinā śaśāṅkadhavalāḥ spaṣṭāṭṭahāsā niśā
eko vā divasaḥ payodamalino yāyānmama prāvṛṣi ||99||(93)
children.translated_text: 'From this day forth, if I should ever again, even in brief, take up the very name of pride or anything else with a deceitful and wicked mind — then without her alone may the nights, white as moonlight, pass with loud laughter, or may even a single rain-clouded day of the monsoon pass for me.' // 99 // (93)

children.text:
idaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ priyatama tanu śvetamatha kiṃ
gamiṣyāmo yāmo bhavatu gamanenātha bhavatu |
purā yenāvaṃ me ciramanusṛtā cittapadavī
sa evānyo jātaḥ sakhi paricitāḥ kasya puruṣāḥ ||100||(94)
children.translated_text: 'This is dark, dark, O dearest — is this body then white? Shall we go? Let us go — let it be with going, or let it be [without].' He who once thus long followed the path of my heart has now become a stranger — O friend, whose are these men who were once so intimate? // 100 // (94)

children.text:
caraṇapatanaṃ sakhyālāpā manoharacāṭavaḥ
kṛśataratanorgāḍhāśleṣo haṭhātparicumbanam |
iti hi capalo mānārambhastathāpi hi notsahe
hṛdayadayitaḥ kāntaḥ kāmaṃ kimatra karomyaham ||101||(95)
children.translated_text: Falling at [my] feet, the conversations of friends, charming sweet words, the tight embrace of [his] ever more emaciated body, a forceful kiss — thus indeed the onset of pride is fickle; yet I cannot [resist] — the beloved is dear to [my] heart; let desire do what it will — what can I do about it? // 101 // (95)

children.text:
ahaṃ tenāhūtā kimapi kathayāmīti vijane
samīpe cāsīnā sarasahṛdayatvādavahitā |
tataḥ karṇopānte kimapi vadatāghrāya vadanaṃ
gṛhītā dharmille sakhi sa ca mayā gāḍhamadhare ||102||(98)
children.translated_text: 'I was called by him; I shall say something,' — thus in a secluded place, sitting near [him], I was attentive due to the tenderness of [my] heart. Then, as he whispered something at my ear and smelled my face, O friend, he was seized by [me] at his hair — and he [seized] me firmly at the lip. // 102 // (98)

children.text:
cakṣuḥprītiprasakte manasi paricaye cintyamānābhyupāye
rāge yāte'tibhūmiṃ vikasati sutarāṃ gocare dūtikāyāḥ |
āstāṃ dūreṇa tāvatsarabhasadayitāliṅganānandalābhas
tadgehopāntarathyābhramaṇamapi parāṃ nirvṛtiṃ santanoti ||103||(100)
children.translated_text: When the mind is absorbed in the delight of the eyes, when intimacy has grown, when the stratagem is being contemplated, when passion has gone to its extreme, when [the affair] has fully blossomed into the domain of a go-between — let alone the joy of the impetuous embrace of the beloved from afar; even wandering in the lane near her house bestows supreme bliss. // 103 // (100)

children.text:
kānte talpamupāgate vigalitā nīvī svayaṃ bandhanād
vāso viślathamekhalāguṇadhṛtaṃ kiṃcinnitambe sthitam |
etāvatsakhi vedmi sāmpratamahaṃ tasyāṅgasaṅge punaḥ
ko'yaṃ kāsmi rataṃ nu vā kathamiti svalpāpi me na smṛtiḥ ||104||(101)
children.translated_text: When the beloved approached the bed, my girdle-string fell loose of itself; my garment, held only by the belt's thread, barely remained upon my hips. This much, my friend, I know now. But in the union of his body with mine — who is he? Who am I? Was love-making achieved? And how? — I have not even the slightest memory. (104)

children.text:
prāsāde sā diśi diśi ca sā pṛṣṭhataḥ sā puraḥ sā
paryaṅke sā pathi pathi ca sā tadviyogāturasya |
haṃho cetaḥ prakṛtiraparā nāsti me kāpi sā sā
sā sā sā sā jagati sakale ko'yamadvaitavādaḥ ||105||(102)
children.translated_text: On the terrace she is; in every direction she is; behind she is, before she is; on the couch she is; on every path she is — for one tormented by her separation. Alas, O heart! There is no other nature for me — she, she, she, she, she, she — in the entire world, what is this doctrine of non-duality? (105)

children.text: Verses found in Arjunavarmadeva's version not found here
children.translated_text: [Verses found in Arjunavarmadeva's version not found here.]

children.text: aṅgulyagranakhena bāṣpasalilaṃ vikṣipya vikṣipya kiṃ
children.translated_text: Flicking away the tear-drops again and again with the tip of your fingernail —

children.text: tūṣṇīṃ rodiṣi kopane bahutaraṃ phūtkṛtya rodiṣyasi |
children.translated_text: Why do you weep in silence? If you are angry, you should weep more, with louder sobs.

children.text: yasyāste piśunopadeśavacanairmāne'tibhūmiṃ gate
children.translated_text: She whose jealous pride has reached its furthest extreme through the words of a malicious gossip's instruction —

children.text: nirviṇṇo'nunayaṃ prati priyatamo madhyasthatāmeṣyate ||(5)
children.translated_text: Your most beloved, wearied of reconciliation, will now adopt indifference. (5)

children.text: tadvaktrābhimukhaṃ mukhaṃ vinamitaṃ dṛṣṭiḥ kṛtā pādayos
children.translated_text: My face was bowed down facing his face; my gaze was fixed upon his feet;

children.text: tasyālāpakutūhalākulatare śrotre niruddhe mayā |
children.translated_text: My ears, all confused with the eagerness of his words, were blocked by me;

children.text: pāṇibhyāṃ ca tiraskṛtaḥ sapulakaḥ svedodgamo gaṇḍayoḥ
children.translated_text: With my hands too he was pushed away — yet goosebumps [arose], and sweat broke out on my cheeks.

children.text: sakhyaḥ kiṃ karavāṇi yānti śatadhā yatkañcuke sandhayaḥ ||(11)
children.translated_text: Friends, what shall I do? The seams of my bodice are bursting in a hundred places! (11)

children.text: nāpeto'nunayena yaḥ priyasuhṛdvākyairna yaḥ saṃhṛto
children.translated_text: That [pride] which was not abandoned through supplication, which was not removed by the words of dear friends,

children.text: yo dīrghaṃ divasaṃ viṣahya viṣamaṃ yatnātkathaṃciddhṛtaḥ |
children.translated_text: Which was somehow maintained with effort through a long, difficult day,

children.text: anyonyasya hṛte mukhe nihitayostiryakkathaṃciddṛśoḥ
children.translated_text: When, faces turned toward each other, their sidelong gazes somehow met —

children.text: sa dvābhyāmativismṛtavyatikaro māno vihasyojjhitaḥ ||(42)
children.translated_text: That pride, its protocol completely forgotten by both, was laughingly abandoned. (42)

children.text: rātrau vāribharālasāmbudaravodvignena jātāśruṇā
children.translated_text: At night, by a traveler alarmed by the rumbling of clouds heavy with rain, and weeping,

children.text: pānthenātmaviyogaduḥkhapiśunaṃ gītaṃ tathotkaṇṭhayā |
children.translated_text: A song was sung in longing, revealing the anguish of separation from the self [beloved];

children.text: āstāṃ jīvitahāriṇaḥ pravasanālāpasya saṃkīrtanaṃ
children.translated_text: Let alone the telling of conversation about the life-threatening journey abroad —

children.text: mānasyāpi jalāñjaliḥ sarabhasaṃ lokena datto yathā ||(54)
children.translated_text: Even to jealous pride, a water-offering [of farewell] was swiftly given by the [whole] world. (54)

children.text: capalahṛdayae kiṃ svātantryāttathā gṛhamāgataś
children.translated_text: O fickle-hearted one, what of your independence? Thus he came home,

children.text: caraṇapatitaḥ premārdrārdraḥ priyaḥ samupekṣitaḥ |
children.translated_text: Fallen at your feet, drenched and tender with love — and the beloved was ignored.

children.text: tadidamadhunā yāvajjīvaṃ nirastasukhodayā
children.translated_text: So now, for the rest of your life, with all hope of happiness cast off,

children.text: ruditaśaraṇā durjātānāṃ sahasva ruṣāṃ phalam ||(56)
children.translated_text: Take refuge in weeping, and endure the fruit of the ill-born's anger! (56)

children.text: āstāṃ viśvasanaṃ sakhīṣu viditābhiprāyasāre jane
children.translated_text: Let alone trusting my friends — among people who understand every intention —

children.text: tatrāpyarpayituṃ dṛśaṃ suracitāṃ śaknomi na vrīḍayā |
children.translated_text: Even to them I cannot direct a well-composed glance, out of shame.

children.text: loko'pyeṣa paropahāsacaturaḥ sūkṣmeṅgitajño'pyalaṃ
children.translated_text: And this world too is skilled in mocking others, knowing subtle gestures all too well.

children.text: mātaḥ kaṃ śaraṇaṃ vrajāmi hṛdaye jīrṇo'nurāgānalaḥ ||(63)
children.translated_text: Mother, to whom shall I turn for refuge? The fire of love smolders deep in my heart. (63)

children.text: analpacintābharamohaniścalā vilokyamānaiva karoti sādhvasam |
children.translated_text: Still with the weight of immense thought, bewildering even to see, inspiring awe —

children.text: svabhāvaśobhānatimātrabhūṣaṇā tanustaveyaṃ bata kiṃ nu sundari ||(65)
children.translated_text: Her natural beauty her sole ornament, not excessively adorned — alas, whose body is this, O beautiful one? (65)

children.text: iti priye pṛcchati mānavihvalā kathaṃcidantardhṛtabāṣpagadgadam |
children.translated_text: When the beloved asked thus, she, overwhelmed by jealous pride, with tears somehow held back, her voice choking,

children.text: na kiṃcidityeva jagāda yadvadhūḥ kiyanna tenaiva tayāsya varṇitam ||(66)
children.translated_text: 'Nothing,' the bride barely whispered — and by that very word, was not everything told by her to him? (66)

children.text:
anālocya premṇaḥ pariṇatimanādṛtya suhṛdas
tvayākāṇḍe mānaḥ kimiti sarale preyasi kṛtaḥ |
samākṛṣṭā hyete virahadahanodbhāsuraśikhāḥ
svahastenāṅgārāstad alamadhunāraṇyaruditaiḥ ||112(?)||(80)
children.translated_text: Without considering the consequences of love, without heeding your friends, you, O guileless one, have adopted jealous pride against your beloved for no reason. For these blazing flame-tips of the fire of separation have been pulled out — coals by your own hand! Enough now with this crying in the wilderness! (112)
(<s>Subhāṣitāvali</s> 1170; <s>Saduktikarṇāmṛta</s> 2.42.1, <s>Sūktimuktāvalī</s> 56.9, <s>Subhāṣitāvalī</s> 659)
